papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Antifibrinolytic Agent: Synthesis and Characterization of Cocrystal and Salts of Tranexamic Acid
papers.abstract: Abstract Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a potent antifibrinolytic agent with poor oral bioavailability (∼35–40%) due to its high polarity and zwitterionic nature, while physicochemical factors, including its structural instability, further hinder its absorption. In this study, the crystal engineering concept is applied to enhance the physicochemical properties of TXA through targeted structural modifications, resulting in the synthesis of pharmaceutically stable cocrystal and salt forms. The application of supramolecular synthon design, pKa rule, and structural geometry (molecular mimicry), resulted in the rational design, synthesis, and structural characterization of eight binary multicomponent forms of TXA: a TXA-adipate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-salicylate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-picolinate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-acetaminophen cocrystal hydrate, monoclinic space group P21; a TXA-malonate salt, orthorhombic space group Pbca; a TXA-maleate salt hydrate, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-malate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; and a TXA-citrate salt, triclinic space group P1̅ These multicomponent forms were obtained via different hydrogen bonding interactions, some of them charge-assisted (N–H···O, N+–H···O–, O–H···O, and O–H···O–) between NH2 and/or −OH groups of TXA and the carboxyl (−C(O−)═O) functional groups of the coformers. In the cocrystals, TXA exists as zwitterions (zero charge), whereas in the salts, it carries a positive charge due to the protonation of its carboxylic (−COOH) and ammonium (−NH3+) groups. The NH3+ to COO– charge-assisted H-bond provides stabilization to both the coformer COO– as well as the TXA’s NH3+. Solid-state characterization using Raman and FT-Raman spectroscopy, thermal techniques (DSC), and X-ray diffraction analysis (powder and single-crystal XRD) supports and confirms the structural novelty. The superior stability profiles of the new TXA cocrystal and salts under standard conditions (40 °C ± 2 °C, 75% ± 5% RH) establish an improved structure–property profile compared to pure TXA.

papers.title: Polyurethane Recycling Using Catalytic Pyrolysis: Insights into Catalyst Stability
papers.abstract: Abstract Polyurethanes are widely used in many applications because of their versatility. However, efficient recycling remains challenging. Recent findings indicate that aniline recovery from rigid polyurethane foams via catalytic pyrolysis with an alumina-based catalyst is an attractive option. Techno-economic analyses showed that catalyst costs are a major factor and that catalyst recycling is essential. Here, we report an extensive study on the recyclability of a selected alumina-based catalyst (Puralox 5/200) for the catalytic pyrolysis of PUR. Experiments with fresh and spent catalysts in a batch-operated staged free-fall reactor at gram scale (3.0 g nPUR, catalyst-to-feed ratio: 1 to 1, 550 °C) using virgin PUR showed differences in activity and chemoselectivity for aniline, indicative of catalyst deactivation. Spent catalyst characterization (TGA–MS, TEM–EDX, N2 physisorption, TPD, and XRD) showed hard coke (14.4 wt %) on the catalyst. Catalyst regeneration was successfully demonstrated using an oxidative treatment at 550 °C, though some irreversible deactivation, including loss in acidity and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area, as well as inorganic accumulation, was observed after five regeneration/recycles. Additional experiments to assess catalyst performance after multiple regeneration-recycles were carried out on a milligram scale in a tandem microreactor coupled to GC–MS/FID (catalyst-to-feed ratio of 5:1 at 550 °C), using rigid polyurethane (nPUR) and a contaminated end-of-life (EOL) feed. With nPUR, catalyst performance for aniline and toluidine formation declined in the first 4 cycles, then stabilized at half the original activity for 28 cycles, and finally dropped to very low levels. For EOL PUR, catalyst performance over multiple runs was significantly worse, and the catalyst was inactive after 18 cycles. We characterized the spent catalysts from both PUR feeds (a.o TEM–EDX), which showed that inorganic impurity accumulation contributes to catalyst deactivation.

papers.title: Putting PASPT2 on a Firmer Basis
papers.abstract: Abstract The recently proposed partial-active-space (PAS) multistate second-order perturbation theory (PASPT2) [Precision Chemistry 4, 997 (2026)] features connected amplitudes and a connected and closed intermediate Hamiltonian. Despite these hallmarks, PASPT2 (denoted as PASPT2H from now on) is not strictly size-extensive, as originally thought (and numerically confirmed), albeit strictly size-consistent. Nevertheless, PASPT2 is near-extensive for the states with major projections on the chosen PASM0. This becomes more transparent upon introducing PASPT2X, a strictly size-extensive variant. Compared with the intruder-prone PASPT2X, the intruder-free PASPT2H merely neglects second-order corrections that are important only for those states with major projections on the orthogonal complement RX of M0 within the closed space MX ( =M0⊕RX). Such states are usually not supported by the chosen finite one-particle basis set. The weak violation of size-extensivity is therefore numerically insignificant for the target states supported by M0, reinforcing the theoretical basis of PASPT2H.

papers.title: A Self-Healing Adhesive Exploiting Hydrogen-Bonding Interactions and Aromatic Disulfide Units in Energetic Composites
papers.abstract: Energetic composites with high solid content are prone to microcracking and interfacial debonding, which can compromise mechanical integrity and service reliability. To address these long-standing durability challenges, herein, a self-healing polyurethane with hydrogen bonds and disulfide bonds (PUHD) was designed by integrating hydrogen-bond reorganization with dynamic disulfide-bond exchange. PUHD was synthesized using polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG) as the soft segment and isophorone diisocyanate (IPDI) and 4,4′-dihydroxydiphenyl disulfide (DHDPS) as hard-segment components. FT-IR, Raman, XRD, GPC, and DSC analyses confirmed the successful construction of a predominantly amorphous dual dynamic network with suitable chain mobility and thermal stability for energetic-composite applications. The neat PUHD exhibited a hardness of 0.94 MPa and a storage modulus of 3.15 MPa at 20 °C and 5 Hz; surface cracks disappeared within 24 h at ambient temperature, and the storage-modulus recovery reached approximately 97%. In sample filler-containing composites, increasing solid content enhanced hardness and modulus but restricted polymer-chain mobility, thereby slowing crack repair and reducing healing recovery. In nitrocellulose/nitroglycerin (NC/NG)-containing composites, the visible crack closure could be achieved within 24 h, while maintaining useful mechanical properties after self-healing. Notably, JQ-e showed the highest initial hardness of 2.69 MPa and retained 2.19 MPa after healing. These findings collectively demonstrate that the synergistic dynamic network not only enables efficient room-temperature crack repair but also preserves adequate mechanical reinforcement, thus offering a viable pathway toward more reliable energetic-composite formulations.

papers.title: A Right to Delegate to AI: The Regulatory Safety Halo and the Acceleration of Agentic Consumer Markets
papers.abstract: Abstract The European Law Institute’s Guiding Principles and Model Rules on Digital Assistants for Consumer Contracts (DACC) propose a right for consumers to use digital assistants in business-to-consumer relations. The DACC’s definition encompasses consumer AI agents (CAIAs), which use AI-generated outputs to determine transactionally relevant matters left open by consumers and initiate or perform transactional actions. The article examines two concerns. First, recognition and safeguards may create a regulatory safety halo, causing consumers to overestimate CAIAs’ technical reliability and the effectiveness of remedies for unwanted outcomes. Second, recognition may accelerate agentic markets, disproportionately benefit incumbents in adjacent digital markets, and foster concentration, to which the DMA and EU competition law provide only partial responses. Legislation should therefore first establish essential rules governing delegation, responsibility and market contestability. Technical implementation may be entrusted to European standardisation bodies, but the Commission’s request should define tasks precisely and maximise transparency and balanced stakeholder participation to mitigate legitimacy concerns. Only once CAIAs are sufficiently reliable and the legal framework more mature should the right to use a CAIA be recognised.

papers.title: Chitosan–Silica Composites: Effect of Polymer Loading and Immobilization Strategy on Surface Structure and Ni(II)/Co(II) Adsorption
papers.abstract: In this work, the effects of chitosan loading and immobilization strategy on the structure and Ni(II) and Co(II) adsorption properties of chitosan–silica composites were studied. To examine the effect of polymer loading, CS/SiO2 composites containing 5–20 wt.% chitosan were prepared by pH-induced precipitation of chitosan onto pristine SiO2. The effect of the immobilization strategy was investigated using an alternative approach involving preliminary functionalization of SiO2 with APTES followed by chitosan deposition. The obtained materials were characterized by TGA, elemental analysis, FTIR spectroscopy, nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis, SEM, and XPS. Direct precipitation of chitosan onto SiO2 resulted in the formation of smaller polymer-containing domains on the silica surface compared with the large agglomerates of pristine chitosan, while regions retaining the characteristic morphology of the silica support remained visible. Chitosan modification improved metal-ion adsorption already at a loading of 5 wt.%. Further increasing the chitosan content to 20 wt.% produced a comparatively smaller additional effect. Preliminary APTES functionalization promoted a more uniform surface morphology of CS/SiO2–APTES compared with directly prepared CS/SiO2. These morphological differences were accompanied by differences in the spectral response of the composites following metal adsorption. CS/SiO2–APTES exhibited smaller shifts in the main N 1s XPS component and almost no change in the silanol-related FTIR band, in contrast to the more pronounced changes observed for CS/SiO2. The directly prepared composite also exhibited faster initial metal uptake. Nevertheless, both composites showed relatively similar equilibrium metal uptake values. These findings highlight the importance of considering polymer organization and surface chemistry when designing supported polymer composites for adsorption and other potential applications.

These findings highlight the importance of considering polymer organization and surface chemistry when designing supported polymer composites for adsorption and other potential applications.

papers.title: Development of a magnetite functionalized cow horn pumice biocomposite for hexavalent chromium removal
papers.abstract: Abstract A magnetite-functionalized cow horn/pumice (Fe 3 O 4 –CH/P) biocomposite was synthesized via in situ co-precipitation and evaluated for the removal of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) from aqueous solutions. A multifunctional adsorbent was engineered by integrating keratin-rich cow horn with highly porous pumice and incorporating magnetite, thereby enhancing its physicochemical properties and enabling efficient magnetic separation. To fully characterize the magnetite-functionalized biocomposite, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) were all employed. At optimized adsorption conditions (pH 3, contact time 120 min, 2 g per100 mL solution (20 g·L − 1 ) dosage), batch adsorption tests showed a very high removal efficiency (> 99.8%). This demonstrates the material’s high affinity for oxyanion species of Cr(VI). The adsorption data are well predicted by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R 2 = 0.99926), indicating that surface-mediated interactions are crucial to the adsorption process. It was determined through isotherm analysis that the Langmuir model provided a better fit (R 2 = 0.9994, a maximum capacity of 15.34 mg·g − 1 ), indicating that homogeneous active sites with a maximum capacity of 15.34 mg·g − 1 and monolayer adsorption are the dominant mechanism. The adsorption process is regulated by electrostatic attraction, surface complexation, and potential redox interactions. According to the results, the magnetite-functionalized cow horn/pumice (Fe 3 O 4 –CH/P) bio-composite is environmentally friendly and a highly effective adsorbent for treating water contaminated with chromium.

papers.title: Thermal Phase Behavior, Structure, Acidity, and Quantum Chemical Insights into Novel Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride (HACl)-Methanesulfonic Acid (MSA) Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract The present study undertakes the first characterization of hydroxylamine hydrochloride (HACl)-methanesulfonic acid (MSA) deep eutectic solvents (DESs), a new generation of sustainable, dual-functional solvents with exceptionally strong acidic and inherently reduced properties. Employing FTIR, Raman, and NMR spectroscopy, the nature of HACl-MSA DESs’ molecular interactions was probed with varying molar ratios between 1:4 and 1:8. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed composition-dependent phase behavior, transitioning from an amorphous glass-forming liquid at 1:4 (Tg = −89 °C, peak at 85.87 °C) to congruent melting at 1:5 (Tm = +5.43 °C). For 1:6 to 1:8 formulations, invariant eutectic behavior was observed with a shared solidus transition at about −53.80 °C and a clear melting range ending between −45.91 and −39.21 °C. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of a homogeneous, single-phase protic DES characterized by a robust, shielded hydroxylammonium core ([NH3OH]+) at 9.87–9.88 ppm and a dynamic acid proton pool that shifts downfield from 13.19 to 13.63 ppm. This shifting resonance directly reflects a tunable macroscopic acidity driven by the expansion of the MSA-MSA hydrogen-bonded network. Quantitative Hammett measurements (H0), determined via UV–vis spectroscopy, demonstrated significant acidity, reaching −6.116 at the 1:8 ratio. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis also confirmed the results, revealing a greater internal thermodynamic stability for the 1:5 ratio with a |ΔEint| = 4.280 eV. However, conceptual DFT descriptors, including a smaller energy gap (7.324 eV), a larger global softness value of 0.137 eV–1, and a more negative chemical potential (−4.506 eV), highlight the 1:4 ratio as a promising theoretical candidate for further evaluation in metal coordination processes. While these electronic metrics suggest a highly polarizable microenvironment, direct extraction yields, leaching kinetics, viscosity, and selectivity require future experimental validation. Through correlations established between molecular structure, frontier orbital analysis, and macroscopic Brønsted acidity trends, HACl–MSA DESs are highlighted as promising candidate platforms for potential application in hydrometallurgical leaching processes. However, definitive claims regarding selective metal extraction, long-term stability, recyclability, and environmental sustainability require comprehensive future experimental evaluation.

Density functional theory (DFT) analysis also confirmed the results, revealing a greater internal thermodynamic stability for the 1:5 ratio with a |ΔEint| = 4.280 eV. However, definitive claims regarding selective metal extraction, long-term stability, recyclability, and environmental sustainability require comprehensive future experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Characterization of PLA–hemp biocomposites produced by hot-pressing
papers.journal: Turkish Journal of Forestry | Türkiye Ormancılık Dergisi
papers.abstract: This study investigates the thermal, chemical, physical, morphological, and mechanical properties of hot-pressed PLA-hemp biocomposites produced without compatibilizers. Hemp particles below 75 µm were composed of PLA at 3%, 6%, and 9 wt%, and neat PLA was evaluated in both granular and extruded forms. The composition was compounded using a twin-screw extruder and converted into plates by hot pressing. TGA showed that extrusion slightly improved the thermal stability of neat PLA, whereas hemp addition reduced degradation temperatures. DSC results demonstrated that hemp fibers increased earlier crystallization and the crystallinity of the PLA matrix. FTIR spectra showed that the interaction between PLA and hemp was mainly physical but there is no evidence of new chemical bond formation. Water absorption and thickness swelling increased with hemp content, reaching the highest values in PLA-H9. Surface roughness was significantly affected by sample type, while tensile and flexural strengths decreased after hemp incorporation. SEM images depicted fiber pull-out, interfacial debonding, and micro voids, confirming limited matrix–fiber adhesion. Overall, hemp addition improved bio-based content but reduced strength without compatibilization.
papers.summary: This study investigates the thermal, chemical, physical, morphological, and mechanical properties of hot-pressed PLA-hemp biocomposites produced without compatibilizers. TGA showed that extrusion slightly improved the thermal stability of neat PLA, whereas hemp addition reduced degradation temperatures. DSC results demonstrated that hemp fibers increased earlier crystallization and the crystallinity of the PLA matrix.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted micro-solid-phase extraction using a MIL-53(Al)/Diaion SP-850 composite for trace determination of erythrosine in food and environmental samples
papers.journal: International Journal of Environmental & Analytical Chemistry
papers.abstract: In this work, a dispersive microsolid phase extraction and determination of erythrosine from water, food and environmental samples was performed. A MIL-53(Al)/Diaion SP-850 composite was prepared and characterised by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET). Micro-solid phase extraction parameters, such as pH, adsorbent amount, adsorption and desorption duration, sonication time, sample volume, eluent type and volume were investigated before the application of the method to real samples. Buffer pH 3.0 phosphate, 10 mg of adsorbent, 60 seconds for adsorption, 3 min for desorption, sample volume of 40 mL and 1 mL absolute ethanol were the optimum conditions resulted from this investigation. Along with the optimisation of the technique, the environmentally friendliness and environment sustainability of the method, namely, Analytical GREEnness Metric Approach (AGREE) and Analytical Greenness Metric for Sample Preparation (AGREEprep) and the Bluenness evaluation (BAGI) were evaluated demonstrating 0.68, 0.75, and 60.0 respective scores. Combining with UV–vis spectrophotometer, the developed ultrasonic-assisted dispersive micro-solid phase extraction method exhibited a linear range of 2.4–3000 µg L−1, low detection limit of 0.80 µg L−1 and a preconcentration factor (40). The method was applied for preconcentration and separation of erythrosine in food and environmental samples presented extraction recovery values ranging 91–102% with relative standard deviation of 4.2%.

papers.title: Highly Tunable Thermal Properties of Multifunctional Thiol‐Ene Networks Derived From Sugar‐Based Monomers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional sugar monomers offer a variety of structural scaffolds for the formation of thiol‐ene networks. Eleven allylated sugars, each having a nominal number of functionalities ranging from 4 to 11, were combined with seven dithiols that were structurally different to produce 77 thiol‐ene networks. Network formation was assessed by ATR‐FTIR, gel‐fraction, and swelling measurements, whereas the thermal and dynamic mechanical analyses indicated that the glass‐transition temperatures T g were in the range from −45°C to 53°C, the midpoint degradation temperatures were between 277°C and 378°C, and the rubbery storage moduli at 100°C were between 3 and 155 MPa. The sugar scaffolds with higher‐functionality generally increased the ranges of the rubbery modulus, the DMA‐derived apparent elastic‐strand density, T g , and relaxation breadth, although the extent of these effects depended strongly on the structure of the dithiol. Analysis based on composition demonstrated that the T g ‐ v c ,app relationship differed in the various dithiol series rather than following a general high‐density plateau. Examination of E ′, E ″, and tan delta showed that there were composition‐dependent differences in relaxation breadth. The sugar and the dithiol structure provide complementary structural parameters for adjusting the thermal and thermomechanical response of multifunctional sugar‐derived thiol‐ene networks.

papers.title: Preparation and evaluation of chitosan-pectin hydrogel films incorporated with Aloe vera-mediated ZnO (AV-ZnO) for diabetic wound healing
papers.abstract: Abstract: Background: Diabetic wounds are challenging due to delayed healing, inflammation, oxidative stress and bacterial infections, which conventional dressings often inadequately address. Objectives: To develop and characterize Aloe vera-mediated ZnO-loaded chitosan-pectin composite hydrogel films and evaluate their physicochemical, antibacterial, antioxidant, and in-vivo wound-healing efficacy in streptozotocin-induced diabetic male Wistar rat. Methods: AV-ZnO was synthesized using Aloe vera gel extract and incorporated into CS/PT hydrogels via solution casting to formulate three groups: PC (without AV-ZnO), PCG-1 (10 mg AV-ZnO), and PCG-2 (20 mg AV-ZnO). Physicochemical characterization included FTIR, SEM, AFM, TGA, gel fraction, contact angle, and tensile testing. Antibacterial activity was assessed against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli via disk diffusion, and antioxidant activity via DPPH radical-scavenging assay. In-vivo wound-healing efficacy was evaluated in streptozotocin-induced diabetic male Wistar rats (N = 24, n = 6/group) across four groups: untreated control, gentamicin-treated control, topical PCG-2, and exploratory oral PCG-2 hydrogel. Results: AV-ZnO incorporation improved tensile strength (10.1 MPa for PCG-2), hydrophilicity, gel fraction, and thermal stability. PCG-2 exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of 28 mm against S. aureus and 20 mm against E. coli, attributed to AV-ZnO (Zn²⁺ release kinetics not evaluated). Antioxidant activity rose concentration-dependently, with PCG-2 showing 60.33% radical scavenging at 0.6 mg/mL. In-vivo, topical PCG-2 showed the highest wound contraction (89.09% ± 0.61 %, p < 0.05 vs. control) by day 15, surpassing exploratory oral treatment (72.84% ± 0.65%) and gentamicin (topical treated group) (83.77% ± 0.25%). Histology indicate improved re-epithelialization and collagen organization with topical treatment versus controls.

papers.title: Bio‐Based Citric Acid‐Cured Epoxy Shape Memory Composites: Effect of Mineral Fillers on Thermal and Shape Memory Performance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of sustainable thermosetting polymers with thermo‐responsive shape memory capability has attracted increasing attention due to their potential applications in smart materials and advanced engineering systems. In this study, bio‐based citric acid was employed as an alternative curing agent for epoxy resin to fabricate thermo‐responsive shape memory epoxy composites. The thermal properties, as well as shape memory behavior of the composites were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analysis and bending tests, respectively. The effects of polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a plasticizing agent in addition to sepiolite and colemanite as mineral reinforcing fillers on the thermal and shape memory properties of the epoxy composites were systematically investigated. The incorporation of PEG improved the chain mobility of the epoxy network, enabling decreased T g and enhanced shape recovery behavior. The optimized composites exhibited excellent thermo‐responsive shape memory performance, achieving high shape recovery ratios with rapid recovery response under thermal stimulation. The obtained results demonstrate that citric acid‐cured epoxy composites reinforced with natural mineral fillers provide a promising sustainable platform for the development of high‐performance shape memory materials.

papers.title: Multiphysics Modeling of Thermo-viscoelastic Damage in Functionally Graded Abradable Coatings with Probabilistic Geometric Tolerance Analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract In aircraft engines, functionally graded abradable coatings are used to control blade-tip clearance, but their durability is governed by effects that are often treated separately in existing models, including temperature-dependent viscoelastic softening, progressive damage, deposition-induced microstructural modulation, and geometric tolerances. Models that consider these effects independently may underestimate damage initiation because smooth material gradients evaluated at nominal geometry cannot capture the local stress concentrations produced by microstructural modulation and geometric variability. This study integrates these effects within a unified multiphysics–probabilistic framework. The solved domain is a local through-thickness coating column driven by prescribed strain and temperature histories that include thermal eigenstrain and coating–substrate expansion mismatch. The results show that periodic property modulation increases end-of-cycle damage relative to the monotonic gradient and concentrates the maximum stress within a localized modulation crest. Propagating symmetric geometric tolerances through the coupled solver produces a strongly right-skewed damage distribution and a higher classification-level exceedance probability for the modulated gradient than for the monotonic gradient. This exceedance behavior cannot be obtained from a deterministic analysis performed at nominal geometry. The exceedance probability is also evaluated as a continuous function of the classification level to assess the sensitivity of the comparison to the selected screening criterion. The implementation is verified through spatial and temporal refinement, closed-form unit tests, nested Monte Carlo convergence with Wilson confidence intervals, and a hold-out-validated polynomial response surface. Numerical verification is clearly distinguished from experimental validation, and the simulated case is presented as a generic benchmark rather than an identified material model. The framework links deposition parameters and tolerance bands to damage-exceedance risk, supporting reliability-oriented screening of graded and multilayer coating systems.

papers.title: Best Response Dynamics for Zero-Sum Dynamic Games with Partial-Asymmetric Information
papers.journal: Journal of Guidance Control and Dynamics
papers.abstract: This work studies a class of zero-sum stochastic linear quadratic dynamic games (LQDGs) under partial and asymmetric information. Information asymmetry introduces fundamental challenges related to belief representation and theory of mind, where players must impute belief states and estimates of other players to inform their strategies. Existing work highlights the difficulty of applying a dynamic programming-like decomposition approach to these problems. An alternative approach based on best response dynamics is proposed, which provides insights into belief representation and theory of mind challenges. Explicit expressions for each player’s best response within the class of pure linear dynamic output feedback control strategies are derived, where the internal state dimension of each control is an integer multiple of the system state dimension. As players iteratively update their best responses, they form increasingly higher-order belief states, leading to infinite-dimensional internal states. However, numerical results reveal that the game’s value converges after only a few iterations, suggesting that higher-order belief states provide vanishing benefit. This work further conducts numerical experiments to analyze the impact of asymmetric beliefs, belief orders, relative controllability and observability, and direct feed-through on a linear quadratic pursuit–evasion game’s value.

papers.title: Integrative approach reveals hidden diversity in the Brachionus (Rotifera, Monogononta)
papers.abstract: The phylum Rotifera has many species complexes that require integrative analyses to resolve their taxonomic identity. Brachionus angularis comprises different morphotypes. In Aguascalientes, Mexico, we observed two of these morphotypes coexisting. To explore their species identity, we applied an integrative approach that combined taxonomical, ecological, and molecular data. Our results demonstrate taxonomic differentiation in the lengths of females, males, and diapausing eggs between the two morphotypes. We also observed distinct hatching patterns and clearly different ornamentation in diapausing eggs between the two morphotypes. Genetic variation between one monoclonal culture of each morphotype revealed distances of 18.8% for mitochondrial COI and 13.73% for nuclear ITS1 regions. These marked, concordant divergences in mitochondrial and nuclear markers across the closely related Brachionus species, together with diagnostic morphological and ecological differences, support the recognition of the two morphotypes as distinct species. Accordingly, we describe Brachionus agsensis sp. nov. and Brachionus hydrocalidensis sp. nov. as new species.

papers.title: Properties of Cellulose Nanocrystals Extracted Using Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) are biosourced colloidal building blocks that have attracted significant scientific attention due to their unique properties, such as high mechanical strength, biodegradability, nontoxicity, and potential for sustainable material development. Acidic hydrolysis utilizing strong acids, mainly sulfuric acid, remains the predominant method for CNC production on both laboratory and commercial scales. However, this approach involves challenges associated with the use of corrosive reagents, acid neutralization, and extensive purification. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have been proposed as alternative processing media for CNC extraction, with potential advantages including reduced reliance on concentrated mineral acids and opportunities for solvent recovery and recycling. Here, we report a detailed characterization of DES-extracted CNCs and their characteristics and properties contrasted with those of commercial acid-extracted CNCs. The DES-CNCs were dispersible but with lower ζ-potential and typically longer lengths, forming colloidal gels down to low concentrations that prevent the formation of liquid crystalline phases at higher concentrations, while ultrasound application and increased ionic strength were also found to promote aggregation. The mechanical response of these eutectic-extracted CNCs is followed by linear and nonlinear rheometry at different concentrations and is compared to that of commercial sulfuric acid-extracted CNCs.

papers.title: Transforming Pediatric Thoracotomy: The Critical Role of Thoracic Paravertebral Block in Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease
papers.journal: Solo Journal of Anesthesi Pain & Critical Care (SOJA)
papers.abstract: Background: Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease (CCHD) encompasses a range of cardiac anomalies that result in low oxygen levels in the blood. This case report explores the use of Thoracic Paravertebral Block (TPVB) as an effective anesthetic technique in a pediatric patient with multiple congenital heart defects. Case Illustration : We report the case of a 46-day-old male pediatric patient diagnosed with CCHD, including pulmonary atresia and Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA) with Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD) and Atrial Septal Defect (ASD). The patient had previously undergone a right Blalock-Taussig (R-BT) shunt and PDA stenting, during which he experienced cardiac arrest but achieved return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). He was admitted for another operation, thoracotomy and decortication due to trapped pleural effusion and empyema. The intraoperative management included the use of TPVB, which provided effective analgesia and hemodynamic stability throughout the procedure. Discussion: TPVB has been increasingly recognized as a valuable regional anesthetic technique in pediatric cardiac surgery. Its use can mitigate the hemodynamic fluctuations often seen with general anesthesia alone, especially in patients with compromised cardiovascular status. In this case, TPVB facilitated stable anesthesia, reduced the requirement for systemic opioids, and helped manage recurrent episodes of desaturation and bradycardia. Conclusion: TPVB is a viable anesthetic option in pediatric patients with CCHD undergoing thoracic surgery. It offers substantial benefits in terms of hemodynamic stability and pain management, contributing to improved perioperative outcomes in this high-risk population

papers.title: Release factor 3 degradation enhances aminoglycoside-mediated translational readthrough at MECP2 nonsense mutations
papers.abstract: Abstract Premature termination codons (PTCs) in the MECP2 gene are a major cause of Rett syndrome, resulting in truncated proteins and loss of function. Pharmacological induction of translational readthrough (TR) can restore full-length protein, but clinical translation is hindered by the limited efficiency and toxicity of current inducers. Here, we investigated whether targeted degradation of the eukaryotic Release Factor 3a by the small molecules CC-885 or CC-90009 enhances TR at MECP2 PTCs in HeLa cells. Using a dual-fluorescence reporter assay, we found that neither degrader alone significantly increased TR efficiency. However, cotreatment with the TR inducer G418 produced a synergistic effect, resulting in increased TR compared to G418 alone. Although gentamicin, a less toxic TR inducer, led to only weak TR induction on its own, combination with CC-885 resulted in TR levels similar to G418. Combined CC-885 and G418 treatment enabled recovery of full-length MeCP2 protein as well as proper nuclear localization, consistent with functional recovery of the nuclear localization signal. These findings establish eRF3a degradation as a potential strategy to enhance TR and suggest that the combination of aminoglycosides with release factor degraders could provide a less toxic yet effective therapeutic option for PTC-associated disorders.

papers.title: Green synthesis of lanthanum oxide nanoparticles using Stachytarpheta jamaicensis leaf extract for solar driven organic dye degradation and biological applications
papers.abstract: Metal oxide nanoparticles with superior physicochemical properties for environmental and medical applications have been developed due to recent breakthroughs in nanoscience. As part of the study, lanthanum oxide (La 2 O 3 ) nanoparticles were fabricated through the use of a green method, in which leaf extract of Stachytarpheta jamaicensis (L.) Vahl was employed as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent, thus offering a green option instead of traditional chemical methods. The resulting nanoparticles were thoroughly analysed by XRD, SEM, FTIR, UV-Visible spectroscopy, DLS/zeta potential and TG/DTA tests to verify phase purity, morphology, elemental composition, functional groups, particle size distribution, and optical properties. PXRD showed the presence of a crystalline structure with an average crystallite size of 38.52 nm. UV-visible spectroscopy absorption bands at 216 and 233 nm accompanied by an absorption edge at 335 nm revealed a semiconducting optical bandgap of around 2.9 eV. La 2 O 3 nanoparticles (0.5 mg/mL) under solar light exhibit degradation of methylene blue and Congo red at about 94.8% and 93.1%, respectively, with pseudo-first- order rate constants of 0.01134 min − 1 for MB and 0.02046 min − 1 for CR. Hydroxyl (·OH) and superoxide (O₂· − ) radical species were found to be the major reason for the degradation based on trapping experiments. Besides that, La 2 O 3 nanoparticles were shown to have a strong antimicrobial effect on Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Bacillus subtilis , and Staphylococcus aureus . This work indicates that green-synthesized La 2 O 3 nanoparticles have a good prospect of being used for wastewater treatment, Environmental degradation and other related applications in a Biomedical and environmentally friendly way.

papers.title: Exploring supervised and unsupervised methods for brain tumor segmentation in MRI images
papers.abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from MRI images is crucial for diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis. In this study, we compare two fundamentally different approaches to tumor segmentation: a supervised deep learning model (2D U-Net) and an unsupervised clustering algorithm (K-means). We evaluate multiple variants of the 2D U-Net trained on different (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) MRI sequences (FLAIR and T1-Gd), as well as a fine-tuned model adapted across modalities, and compare them with K-means clustering applied separately on both modalities.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis Applications in Improving Engineering Models
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Numerical analysis serves as the fundamental pillar of modern engineering modeling, providing the mathematical and computational tools necessary to transform complex physical equations into practical numerical solutions. This study reviews contemporary applications of numerical analysis in enhancing engineering models, focusing on methodological advancements in solving partial differential equations, data-driven model order reduction techniques, adaptive mesh methods, and machine learning-based surrogate models. The study employs a synthetic analytical approach that combines a review of recent literature with an analysis of empirical results from various numerical methods, addressing hybrid models that integrate traditional techniques with artificial intelligence. The analysis demonstrates that combining traditional numerical analysis methods with artificial intelligence and reduced-order models has revolutionized the ability of engineers to simulate complex multiphysics systems with unprecedented accuracy and computational efficiency; hybrid models have achieved computational speedups ranging from 72 to 522 times compare to traditional methods. Furthermore, the study addresses challenges related to computational cost and solution sensitivity to initial conditions, examining cutting-edge innovative solutions such as physicsinformed neural networks and causality-based learning. The study concludes that future trends in this field are shifting towards the development of hybrid models that combine analytical accuracy with computational speed, with an increasing emphasis on generalization capabilities beyond the training data. This opens up broad prospects for digital engineering and digital twin applications across the industrial, energy, and infrastructure sectors. The study offers a comprehensive perspective on the development of engineering models using advanced numerical analysis techniques and identifies promising future research directions in this vital field.

papers.title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x‐ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP‐based diagnostics, from benchtop to high‐fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

papers.title: Research and Development Process, Regulatory Requirements and Clinical Trial of Medical Devices: A Review within the Framework of the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK) and the European Union (Regulation 2017/745)
papers.abstract: Medical devices encompass a wide range, from simple instruments to complex implants and software, and recent technological advancements have significantly increased both their number and clinical significance. Bringing a medical device from concept to clinical use requires an integrated pathway combining structured research and development, risk management, regulatory compliance, and robust clinical evidence. In the European Union, Regulation 2017/745 (Medical Devices Regulation) superseded previous directives and strengthened the requirements for clinical evaluation, technical certification, post-market surveillance, and traceability. Türkiye has aligned its national framework with this regulation through the Medical Devices Regulation published by the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK). This review addresses the medical device lifecycle from a regulatory and scientific perspective, covering device definition and risk-based classification, the design and development process and the supporting quality and risk management standards, preclinical laboratory and biological evaluation, in vivo studies, and clinical evaluation and clinical research requirements. Particular attention is paid to the alignment between Good Clinical Practices (ISO 14155) and post-market obligations for device research within the Turkish (TITCK) and European (Regulation No. 2017/745) frameworks. Understanding this integrated pathway in the early stages of development is crucial for the efficient, compliant, and patient-centered transfer of medical devices to clinical practice.

papers.title: Hetero-grafting affects sugar and flavonoid accumulation in ‘Misty’ blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum)
papers.abstract: Introduction Grafting can be used in blueberry cultivation to improve soil adaptability and scion fruit quality. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated the effects of rabbiteye blueberry ( Vaccinium virgatum ) ‘Climax’ and ‘Brightwell’ rootstocks on fruit quality, biochemical characteristics, and related gene expression in ‘Misty’ blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum ). Results The fruit quality of ‘Climax’-grafted ‘Misty’ (CM) was superior to that of ‘Brightwell’-grafted ‘Misty’ (BM). CM showed greater scion stem diameter and fruit size, as well as the net photosynthetic rate, and chlorophyll contents in leaves. Notably, LC-MS/MS analysis detected significant increases in specific sugars and flavonoids in CM fruit, with glucose and fructose contents 10.2% and 11.4% higher than BM, respectively. Twenty-four out of the 31 quantified flavonoids were more abundant in CM. In contrast, 26 of the 28 detected amino acids accumulated at higher levels in BM, as did most organic acids. A total of 1,411 differentially expressed genes, including 830 upregulated and 581 downregulated genes, were detected between CM and BM fruit, in which the genes associated with sugar ( VcSWEET12 and VcINV1 ) and flavonoids ( VcF3′H and VcUFGT ) were upregulated in CM fruit. An integrated analysis pinpointed nine transcription factors, including VcWRKY75 and VcWRKY24 , as potential modulators of sugar metabolism and flavonoid biosynthesis. Discussion These findings indicate that different rabbiteye blueberry rootstocks are associated with distinct physiological and metabolic responses in southern highbush blueberry. Compared with ‘Brightwell’, the ‘Climax’ rootstock was more conducive to improving the comprehensive quality of ‘Misty’ blueberry fruit. The results provide candidate molecular targets for dissecting the process of fruit quality formation mediated by rootstock–scion interactions, and they form a basis for high-quality blueberry cultivation.

papers.title: Advances in myopia progression control – from atropine to personalised treatment
papers.abstract: Krótkowzroczność stanowi jedno z największych wyzwań współczesnej okulistyki, a głównym celem jej leczenia jest obecnie nie tylko korekcja wady refrakcji, lecz przede wszystkim zahamowanie progresji i ograniczenie ryzyka rozwoju wysokiej krótkowzroczności. W ostatnich latach strategie terapeutyczne ewoluowały od pojedynczych interwencji do kompleksowego, spersonalizowanego podejścia obejmującego farmakoterapię, zaawansowane technologie optyczne oraz modyfikację czynników środowiskowych. Atropina, szczególnie w niskich stężeniach, pozostaje jedną z najlepiej udokumentowanych metod kontroli progresji, jednak dynamiczny rozwój technologii optycznych umożliwił wprowadzenie nowych rozwiązań, takich jak soczewki H.A.L.T., D.I.M.S., DOT i C.A.R.E., wykorzystujące kontrolowane rozogniskowanie krótkowzroczne. Coraz większe zainteresowanie budzą również innowacyjne metody oparte na modulacji światłem, w tym terapia powtarzanym światłem czerwonym o niskiej intensywności (RLRL) oraz cyfrowa fotobiomodulacja, choć wymagają one dalszej oceny bezpieczeństwa i skuteczności. Istotnym kierunkiem rozwoju pozostaje terapia skojarzona, łącząca różne mechanizmy działania, szczególnie u dzieci z szybką progresją krótkowzroczności. Przyszłość kontroli krótkowzroczności będzie opierać się na indywidualizacji leczenia, uwzględniającej profil ryzyka pacjenta, tempo wydłużania osiowego oraz optymalny dobór metod terapeutycznych.

papers.title: Chitosan coating with Pickering emulsion of cellulose nanofibril/kaffir lime leaf essential oil for gourami fillets preservation
papers.journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Gourami fillets ( Osphronemus goramy ) are susceptible to rapid deterioration during chilled storage. This study developed a chitosan-based edible coating containing a cellulose nanofibril (CNF)-stabilized Pickering emulsion of kaffir lime leaf essential oil (KEO) and evaluated its fish-preservation performance. A CNF concentration of 0.25% was selected as chitosan/CNF/KEO (ChiCK) stabilizer, and comparing with chitosan (Chi), chitosan/Tween 80/KEO (ChiTK). A ChiCK showed the highest zeta potential (57.00 ± 1.04 mV) and inhibition zones of 9.262 ± 0.639 mm, 10.306 ± 0.127 mm, 9.472 ± 0.824 mm, and 8.696 ± 0.260 mm against Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Bacillus cereus , and Staphylococcus aureus respectively. Its application on gourami fillet was able to suppress microbial growth with total plate count of 5.30 ± 0.05 log CFU g −1 , 1.12 log units lower than that of the uncoated fillets by day 2 storage and remined below the maximum limit of safe level (5.70 log CFU g −1 ), although the treatment did not reduce weight loss by day 3. The CNF-stabilized KEO coating therefore had potential for preserving the gourami fillets during chilled storage (5 °C–10 °C).

papers.title: MHD analysis of tangent hyperbolic micropolar fluid flow over a permeable stretching surface
papers.abstract: This investigation analyzes the effects of micropolar tangent hyperbolic hybrid nanofluid flow over a porous stretching sheet. Additionally, the influences of magnetohydrodynamics and heat source/sink effects are also considered into the analysis. The angular momentum equation is employed to examine the micro-rotation characteristics of the fluid flowing, whereas the enhancement in heat transport performance is evaluated through the inclusion of hybrid nanoparticles. These equations are subsequently reduced to a system of ordinary differential equations using suitable similarity transformations. The resulting nonlinear system is solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg 45 (RKF-45) method in conjunction with a shooting technique. The effects of relevant physical parameters are illustrated through graphical representations, highlighting their physical significance. Graphical representations depict the physical significance of relevant parameters. Validation of numerical results is performed by comparing them with previously published data. The main conclusions of the study are as follows: (1) a gradual reduction in fluid velocity is observed with an increase in Weissenberg number $$\:(We=0.0,\:0.5,\:1.0)$$ , and permeability parameter $$\:\:(K=0.0,\:0.4,\:0.8)$$ , while the surface condition parameter is fixed at $$\:n\:=\:0.5$$ , (2) the skin friction coefficient shows a pronounced decrease as the permeability parameter increases $$\:(K=0.0,\:0.5,\:1.0)$$ , (3) the wall couple stress exhibits an increasing trend with rising values of the micro-rotation parameter $$\:({\Psi\:}=0.0,\:2.0,\:4.0)$$ . Owing to the unique rheological behavior, tangent hyperbolic fluids are widely applicable in engineering and biomedical systems, where they facilitate controlled transport in food processing, polymer technology, oil recovery, and blood flow analysis.

The resulting nonlinear system is solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg 45 (RKF-45) method in conjunction with a shooting technique.

papers.title: Design and multiphysics analysis of an active-passive thermal protection strategy for transverse flux induction heating of moving strips
papers.abstract: Transverse flux induction heating (TFIH) offers distinct advantages in the field of metal strip heat treatment. However, optimizing its heating performance and ensuring the stable operation of the inductor requires a comprehensive multiphysics coupled analysis. To address the excessive inductor temperature rise caused by narrow air gaps in novel coil designs during high-temperature strip processing, this paper proposes a thermal protection strategy that combines active internal water cooling with passive composite thermal insulation. Forced water passages inside the hollow copper turns evacuate internal ohmic dissipation, while thin multi-layer ceramic-vacuum boards intercept intense radiative and convective heat fluxes from the moving strip. A finite element model of TFIH for moving strips is developed, accounting for strip motion, temperature-dependent material properties, water cooling, and thermal insulation. This modeling approach is experimentally validated using a low-power diamond-coil prototype. Subsequently, the validated method is applied to simulate a TFIH system featuring a novel dual-hexagonal-coil structure. Results demonstrate that the dual-hexagonal-coil structure significantly improves the thermal uniformity of the strip. Furthermore, the proposed protection measure not only prevents inductor overheating but also minimizes heat loss from the strip, producing a measurable rise in the delivered strip temperature without increasing input power. This study provides a valuable technical framework for the design and optimization of TFIH devices.
papers.summary: Transverse flux induction heating (TFIH) offers distinct advantages in the field of metal strip heat treatment. Subsequently, the validated method is applied to simulate a TFIH system featuring a novel dual-hexagonal-coil structure. Results demonstrate that the dual-hexagonal-coil structure significantly improves the thermal uniformity of the strip.

papers.title: Elapsed irrigation time improves morpho-kinematic classification of lettuce irrigation-stress histories
papers.abstract: Plant movement carries information on water status, but its predictive value may depend on the recent irrigation context in which movement is expressed. Previous lettuce morpho-kinematic (MK) analyses suggested that integrating a precise measurement of elapsed irrigation time ( Δt , defined as the interval from the last irrigation preceding the observation day to the start of imaging, excluding any same-day irrigation) may improve classification, but its contribution was not formally separated from nominal irrigation schedule (which represents a protocol-derived low-resolution Δt proxy). We reanalysed 140 plant-day observations from 24 plants in two controlled-environment experiments using, to isolate the predictive value of Δt , a schedule-balanced binary contrast obtained by grouping well irrigated (FC) and chronic stress (SC) against moderate and severe acute stresses (SM and SS respectively). Penalised logistic models were evaluated with plant-level balanced validation and plant-class balanced log-loss. Adding Δt reduced held-out log-loss from 0.5250 to 0.4836 (ΔLL = 0.0414; 95% CI = [0.0034, 0.0807]), whereas adding nominal schedule did not (ΔLL = −0.0039; 95% CI = [−0.0342, 0.0273]). The estimated Δt benefit remained predominantly positive under stricter validation, while schedule-preserving permutations and redundancy analysis supported an observation-specific contribution beyond schedule. These findings indicate that recent irrigation history can provide useful temporal context for MK-based classification; the underlying physiological mechanism remains unresolved.

Penalised logistic models were evaluated with plant-level balanced validation and plant-class balanced log-loss. These findings indicate that recent irrigation history can provide useful temporal context for MK-based classification; the underlying physiological mechanism remains unresolved.

papers.title: GenTile: Closing the Loop Between LLM Reasoning and Physical Telemetry for Autonomous NPU Graph Tuning
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM) hidden widths—such as the 18 944-dimensional intermediate layer of the Qwen family—are often burst-aligned but not tile-compatible with heterogeneous NPU Cube engines, forcing the compiler to emit a small residual kernel that stalls the pipeline for up to 77% of cycles. Manual tuning does not scale across the growing space of model dimensions, sequence lengths, and operator variants. We present GenTile, a dual-role Research–Development (R&D) agent framework that closes the loop between LLM causal reasoning and on-device telemetry: a Research agent diagnoses bottlenecks from structured profiles, a Development agent materializes hardware-legal descriptors from compiler feedback, and iteration traces accumulate into a reusable knowledge base under an air-gap sandbox. On Ascend 910B, an offline hardware-faithful sandbox loop first demonstrates convergence mechanics; on real pretrained weights, the loop then measures the full multi-objective trade-off—latency, energy, memory, AICore efficiency, and approximation error (ε)—across six projection families from two Qwen generations (Qwen3.5-32B and Qwen2.5-7B). From telemetry alone, the agent deploys lossless sibling-projection fusions (QKV, gate–up) consistent with production inference-engine layouts (1.06–1.16× faster, up to 13% lower energy, ε=0, stable across sequence lengths, layer depths, and both models), and rejects every lossy low-rank rewrite—including a 1.39× lm_head speedup whose measured ε=0.89 exceeds any usable accuracy budget—while validating the Eckart–Young cliff prediction (ε → 0.002 at the tail rank) on structural layers. Baselines, ablations, cross-dimension generalization, and a sandbox loop that matches the geometric Oracle within four generations without exhaustive search further support the framework.
