papers.title: Review on Self Micro-Emulsifying Drug Delivery System
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Poor aqueous solubility, dissolution-limited absorption and variable oral bioavailability remain important obstacles in the development of many modern drug molecules.Self micro-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SMEDDS) are isotropic mixtures of drug, oil, surfactant and co-surfactant that disperse spontaneously in gastrointestinal fluid to form fine oil-inwater microemulsions.This review summarizes the pharmaceutical basis, formulation components, development strategy, characterization requirements, advantages, limitations and recent advances of SMEDDS, with special emphasis on solid SMEDDS, supersaturable SMEDDS and the rational selection of newly approved drugs for future formulation screening.A literature-oriented approach was used to organize information from published work on lipid-based oral formulations, selfemulsifying systems and official novel drug approval lists from 2023 to 2026.The review identifies oil solubilization capacity, surfactant/co-surfactant compatibility, self-emulsification time, globule size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, dilution robustness, precipitation resistance, dissolution behavior and thermodynamic stability as critical variables for successful SMEDDS development.The recent approval of several orally relevant anticancer, anti-inflammatory, metabolic, CNS, antibacterial and antiviral molecules provides opportunities for formulation scientists to screen SMEDDS as a bioavailability-enhancing platform.However, suitability must be established by experimental solubility, dose loading, drug-excipient compatibility, digestion and stability studies.Overall, SMEDDS represents a practical and adaptable lipidbased technology for improving the oral delivery of poorly soluble drugs when developed with systematic excipient screening, quality-by-design principles and careful regulatory control.

papers.title: Heterojunctions for food freshness monitoring: interfacial engineering, sensing mechanisms, and intelligent packaging
papers.abstract: The growing demand for real-time, non-destructive, and intelligent food quality assessment has spurred rapid advances in chemical sensors that monitor freshness deterioration during storage, transportation, and retail. Among emerging sensing platforms, heterojunction-based sensors are particularly attractive because their well-defined interfacial architectures regulate charge transport, surface adsorption, catalytic activation, and signal amplification. These features are highly desirable for detecting volatile spoilage biomarkers, including ammonia (NH 3 ), hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), trimethylamine (TMA), and other bioamines, which are continuously released during the microbial and enzymatic degradation of protein-rich foods such as meat, fish, seafood, and dairy products. This review first elucidates the formation mechanisms of key spoilage biomarkers, including NH 3 , H 2 S, TMA, and other bioamines, in high-protein foods (meat, aquatic products, and dairy products), and clarifies their basis as freshness fingerprints. We then systematically summarize major heterojunction-based sensing platforms, including metal oxide and sulfide heterostructures, noble-metal-modified heterostructures, carbon- and MXene-based hybrids, porous framework-based composites, and conductive polymer heterostructures. Particular attention is given to p–n, n–n, p–p, and Schottky junctions, with a clear distinction between interfacial signal amplification driven by band bending, depletion-layer modulation, and built-in electric fields, and molecular selectivity governed primarily by analyte-dependent surface chemistry, defect sites, catalytic activity, and pore structure. Heterojunction formation enhances signal transduction and response kinetics and may improve selectivity when it preferentially alters the adsorption or reaction pathways of the target analyte relative to interfering species. Furthermore, representative applications in food analysis, intelligent packaging, flexible devices, wireless monitoring, and cold-chain early warning are highlighted to demonstrate the translation from materials design to practical freshness monitoring. Finally, we analyze critical challenges related to humidity and matrix interference, cross-sensitivity, signal drift, reproducibility, food-contact safety, scalable fabrication, standardized evaluation, data reliability, and sustainable integration. This review establishes a mechanistic framework linking spoilage chemistry, heterointerface engineering, sensing performance, and practical deployment, and provides design principles for next-generation intelligent food-freshness monitoring platforms.

papers.title: Machine learning-based segmentation and quantitative histological assessment of bovine liver fibrosis: Comparative performance of three open-source models
papers.abstract: Background and Aim: Conventional semiquantitative histopathological scoring of hepatic fibrosis is affected by interobserver variability and provides limited quantitative information on the spatial distribution and progression of collagen deposition. Machine learning (ML)-based image analysis may provide a reproducible approach for objective fibrosis assessment in veterinary pathology. This study compared three open-source ML models, Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS), Ilastik, and Fiber-ML, for segmentation and quantitative assessment of bovine liver fibrosis and evaluated their diagnostic performance, agreement with METAVIR staging, and computational efficiency. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional observational study included liver samples from 35 cattle diagnosed with hepatic fibrosis according to the clinical sign records. Masson’s trichrome-stained sections were classified according to METAVIR stages F0–F4 (F0 represents normal liver samples, n=7). A total of 525 images were obtained from perisinusoidal, pericentral, and periportal regions. Images from 25 animals (375 images) constituted the training/validation dataset with five-fold cross-validation, whereas images from 10 animals (150 images) formed an independent testing dataset. A similar dataset was annotated by experts to generate manual ground-truth segmentation, and images from the same animal appeared in both training and testing datasets. Model performance was assessed using collagen proportionate area (CPA), Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, correlation with METAVIR scores, and computational-resource requirements. Results: Ilastik and Fiber-ML generally achieved greater segmentation agreement than TWS (p ≤ 0.05), with DSC values reaching 0.91 and 0.92, compared to 0.87 in TWS, depending on the hepatic region. Overall model pixel-level segmentation accuracy ranged from 84.7% to 91.8%, with the highest performance observed in the periportal region. CPA measurements generated by the models showed strong positive correlations with METAVIR stages (ρ = 0.97–0.99). Fiber-ML required substantially less computational resources, while Ilastik recorded fewer software errors than TWS, including shorter training time and lower CPU and RAM utilization. All computational benchmarking was conducted under identical hardware and software conditions. Conclusion: Open-source ML models enabled objective segmentation and quantitative assessment of bovine hepatic fibrosis. Ilastik and Fiber-ML demonstrated strong agreement with expert-derived reference segmentation and fibrosis staging, while Fiber-ML offered additional computational efficiency. These findings support ML-assisted digital histopathology as a future complementary tool for quantifying and spatially characterizing hepatic fibrosis in cattle. Further validation is required before their reproducibility and diagnostic applicability can be established. Keywords: bovine liver fibrosis, collagen proportionate area, digital histopathology, hepatic fibrosis, machine learning, METAVIR staging, segmentation, veterinary pathology.

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Etravirine-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles in Herbal Hydrogel for Sustained Antiviral Delivery
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study was undertaken to formulate and evaluate Etravirine-loaded lipid nanoparticles incorporated into an herbal hydrogel for sustained antiviral drug delivery. Etravirine is an antiretroviral drug used in the treatment of Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type-1 (HIV-1) infection. However, its poor aqueous solubility and limited dissolution may affect its delivery. Therefore, lipid nanoparticles were developed to improve drug incorporation and provide controlled drug release. The study included preformulation studies, drug–excipient compatibility testing, preparation and optimization of lipid nanoparticles, and incorporation of the optimized nanoparticles into an herbal hydrogel. The prepared formulations were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, drug loading, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, drug content, and in-vitro drug release. The optimized lipid nanoparticles showed a particle size of 142.6 ± 4.8 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.218, a zeta potential of −32.8 ± 1.5 mV, an entrapment efficiency of 92.4 ± 1.2%, and drug loading of 8.75 ± 0.24%. Among the nine hydrogel formulations, DF6 showed the best overall results, with a pH of 6.18 ± 0.03, spreadability of 25.3 ± 0.5 g·cm/sec, drug content of 98.8 ± 0.4%, and cumulative drug release of 96.4 ± 0.9% after 24 hours. The drug release profile followed the Higuchi model, indicating diffusion-controlled release. Three-month stability studies showed negligible changes in the evaluated formulation characteristics. The findings indicate that the Etravirine-loaded lipid nanoparticle herbal hydrogel is a promising formulation for sustained drug delivery. Further studies are required to establish its safety, skin penetration, and therapeutic effectiveness.

papers.title: Interfacially Engineered Alginate/Hydroxyapatite Biocomposites With High Strength and Toughness
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the high toughness of cortical bone, we aimed to develop biomass‐based structural materials by hybridizing sodium alginate (ALG‐Na) with hydroxyapatite (HAP) through in situ crystallization. Two protocols were designed: Method A, crystallizing HAP from ALG‐Na in a Na 2 HPO 4 /NaOH mixture; and Method B, crystallizing HAP after ALG‐Na pre‐crosslinking with Ca 2+ in CaCl 2 . Composites synthesized at 25°C–90°C were characterized by thermogravimetric–differential thermal analysis, Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy, X‐ray diffraction, three‐point bending, and scanning electron microscopy. Method B, particularly at 70°C, yielded higher thermal stability, stronger organic–inorganic interactions, and improved mechanical properties. In Method A, ALG‐Na carboxylate groups (COO − ) preferentially bound free Ca 2+ , suppressing HAP interactions. Method B enabled mild HAP crystal growth near calcium alginate, promoting COO − interaction with positively charged HAP a ‐planes. The optimized composite showed 13‐, 8.6‐, and 22.5‐fold higher bending strength ( σ b ), elastic modulus ( E b ), and modulus of toughness ( K f ) than pure ALG‐Na. σ b matched poly(methyl methacrylate) and nylon 66; E b matched glass fiber–reinforced poly(butylene terephthalate). K f remained comparable to softwoods, balancing rigidity and toughness. This study provides guidelines for interfacial control in carboxylate biopolymer/HAP composites and has the potential to contribute to the rational design of high‐performance biomass structural materials.

papers.title: Development and Evaluation of Tizanidine Hydrochloride-Loaded Nano-structured Lipid Carriers in Mucoadhesive Buccal Films for Enhanced Permeation
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate Tizanidine Hydrochloride-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) incorporated into mucoadhesive buccal films for sustained drug delivery. Tizanidine Hydrochloride is a centrally acting muscle relaxant with a short half-life and extensive first-pass metabolism. Nanostructured lipid carriers were prepared using glyceryl monostearate as the solid lipid, Capryol® 90 as the liquid lipid, Tween® 80 as the surfactant, and Poloxamer 188 as the co-surfactant. The optimized NLC formulation, TF4, showed a particle size of 182.3 ± 2.9 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.214 ± 0.012, a zeta potential of −31.6 ± 1.4 mV, entrapment efficiency of 89.6 ± 0.9%, and drug loading of 7.52 ± 0.09%. The optimized NLCs were incorporated into mucoadhesive buccal films using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose E15 and Carbopol 934P. Among the prepared films, BF5 exhibited satisfactory physicochemical and mechanical properties, including a thickness of 0.138 ± 0.004 mm, folding endurance of 174 ± 5 folds, surface pH of 6.18 ± 0.05, and drug content of 98.64 ± 0.72%. The formulation achieved 91.4% cumulative drug release over 8 hours. Release kinetic analysis showed the best fit with the Higuchi model ((R^2 = 0.9982)), suggesting diffusion-controlled release. Three-month stability studies showed that the optimized film retained satisfactory physical and physicochemical characteristics. These findings indicate that NLCbased mucoadhesive buccal films may offer a promising approach for the sustained delivery of Tizanidine Hydrochloride. Further permeation and in-vivo studies are required to establish their therapeutic performance.

papers.title: Strategic Design, Formulation and Optimization of Anastrozole Solid Lipid Nanoparticles for Breast Cancer Therapy
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Anastrozole is a gold-standard postoperative endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal individuals. However, its therapeutic utility is severely restricted, necessitating frequent high-dose systemic administration which triggers severe musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal toxicities. Objectives: The goal of this study was to create, statistically optimize, physicochemically characterize Anastrozole-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (A-LA-SLNs) utilizing lauric acid matrix that can exploit lymphotropic absorption pathways. Materials and Methods: A-LA-SLNs were fabricated using a hot homogenization-ultrasonication technique. To evaluate the influence of the independent variables, we employed a two-factor, three-level Central Composite Design (CCD). Independent variables were lipid concentration and surfactant concentration. Entrapment efficiency, hydrodynamic particle size, and zeta potential were the critical quality attributes. Phyiscochemical characterizations were performed and in vitro release was monitored using dialysis bag diffusion across multiple physiological pH conditions. Results: The optimized A-LA-SLN formulation demonstrated a particle size of 96.90 nm, a robust negative zeta potential of -21.0 mV, and an elevated entrapment efficiency exceeding 85%. FTIR and Raman spectral profiles confirmed structural compatibility and uniform molecular dispersion of Anastrozole within the fatty acid core. In vitro dissolution profiles in simulated intestinal fluids (pH 6.8 and 7.4) demonstrated highly controlled, sustained release kinetics over 24 h compared to immediate, uncontrolled dissolution in conventional commercial tablets. Conclusion: The developed lauric acid-based nanocarrier effectively bypassed the physicochemical limitations of conventional Anastrozole. By offering sustained-release kinetics and leveraging the inherent lymphatic affinity of medium-chain fatty acids, this delivery platform holds strong potential to enhance oral bioavailability and mitigate systemic off-target toxicities in clinical breast cancer management.

papers.title: Engineering pH-Responsive Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Encapsulating Demethylzeylasteral for Targeting PI3K/AKT Signaling in Pancreatic Cancer
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for innovative strategies that improve intracellular drug delivery and target critical survival pathways. The present study investigated a pH-responsive mesoporous silica nanoparticle (MSN) system for encapsulation and delivery of demethylzeylasteral (DMZ), with particular emphasis on modulation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. DMZ-loaded pH-responsive MSNs were prepared and characterized for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, surface area, pore characteristics, drug-loading efficiency, and structural properties. In vitro release studies were performed under physiological and acidic conditions to evaluate pH-responsive drug release. The biological activity of free DMZ, DMZ-loaded MSNs, and pH-responsive DMZ-MSNs was evaluated in pancreatic cancer cells by assessing cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, migration, and invasion. Molecular analysis was performed to determine changes in PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and apoptosis-associated proteins. The optimized pH-responsive DMZ-MSN formulation demonstrated nanoscale characteristics, efficient DMZ encapsulation, and enhanced drug release under acidic conditions. Compared with free DMZ and non-responsive DMZ-loaded MSNs, the pH-responsive formulation exhibited enhanced cellular uptake, greater cytotoxicity, increased apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, and stronger inhibition of migration and invasion. These effects were associated with suppression of phosphorylated PI3K, AKT, and mTOR together with increased Bax and cleaved caspase-3 and reduced Bcl-2 expression. In vivo evaluation further indicated enhanced tumor suppression with an acceptable preliminary safety profile. Collectively, the findings support pH-responsive DMZ-MSNs as a promising nanotherapeutic platform for pancreatic cancer targeting PI3K/AKT-associated survival signaling.

In vivo evaluation further indicated enhanced tumor suppression with an acceptable preliminary safety profile.

papers.title: Inhibition of spontaneous combustion in low-rank coal by facultative anaerobic microflora: reducing oxidizer, increasing retardant and modifying coal structure
papers.abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion is a major mining hazard, causing casualties, economic losses, and environmental damage. Here, an eco-friendly microbial fire prevention technology was proposed. A facultative anaerobic functional microflora was cultivated from coal seam water. Its metabolic characteristics, community structure, and effects on coal properties were investigated under varying initial oxygen concentrations. The microflora rapidly consumed oxygen to below 5% within one day, reaching 1.5% under low-oxygen conditions, while CO 2 concentrations reached 7.51%-14.43%. After microbial treatment, the relative proportions of OH-O ether oxygen hydrogen bonds, alcohol and ether C-O, conjugated C=O, and carboxyl C=O decreased by 17.4%-69.1%, 29.2%-76.8%, 15.1%-81.2%, and 19.0%-36.4%, respectively. Aliphatic branching decreased whereas the relative proportion of aromatic C=C increased. Thermal analysis showed that characteristic temperatures increased by 19.65–32.81 °C, maximum heat release rates decreased by 47.8%-54.2%, and combustion-stage activation energies increased substantially. The dominant genera included Delftia , Clostridium , and Pseudomonas , which potentially involve in complex-compound degradation and support the coal-component degradation under various oxygen conditions. These results suggested that the microflora could effectively inhibit coal spontaneous combustion through oxygen consumption to decrease oxidizer availability, CO 2 production to increase retardant concentration, and coal structural modification to reduce spontaneous combustion propensity. This study established a theoretical foundation for applying microbial technology in mine fire prevention.

This study established a theoretical foundation for applying microbial technology in mine fire prevention.

papers.title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF A POLYHERBAL IMMUNITY BOOSTER TABLET
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The objective of the current study was to standardize and create a polyherbal pill that would increase immunity by containing Withania somnifera, Tinospora cordifolia, Curcuma longa, Zingiber officinale, and Phyllanthus emblica L. The Drugs were found to have acceptable quality characteristics, including foreign matter ranging from 0.36 to 0.55%, drying loss ranging from 5.46 to 7.12%, and total ash values less than 6.24%.The polyherbal mixture was identified by quantitative phytochemical analysis as having 88.5 ± 2.4 mg GAE/g of total phenolics and 55.6 ± 1.8 mg QE/g of total flavonoids, along with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50) of 15.2 ± 0.5 µg/mL that demonstrated 95.4 ± 1.3% of free radical scavenging activity as determined by the DPPH assay.The lack of notable drug-excipient interactions was confirmed by FTIR and DSC analyses.Out of the five wet granulation formulations (F1-F5), F3 was chosen as an optimized batch due to its favorable pre-compression and post-compression properties, such as drug content (98.8±1.1%),hardness (6.3±0.2 kg/cm2), friability (0.54±0.02%), and disintegration time (11.4±0.4 min).The release kinetics of the most optimal formulation, which released 96.4±1.6% drug in cumulative drug release data after 45 minutes, were fitted by the Korsmeyer-Peppas model (R2=0.993).According to the accelerated stability studies, there were no significant changes in the drug content (98.8% to 97.3%) and dissolution (96.4% to 95.1%) under ICH Q1A (R2) conditions (40 ± 2°C/75 ±5% RH), and all spoilage-related quality standards remained well within the acceptable limits specified by pharmacopoeia.Our study's findings show that the optimized polyherbal tablet is pharmaceutically stable and that it may be a viable alternative for a novel oral herbal formulation with immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties.

papers.title: Deep Eutectic Solvents in Organic and Inorganic Transformations: Physicochemical Properties and Potential Pharmaceutical Applications
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs) are emerging as alternative, environmentally friendly solvents to conventional organic solvents due to their low toxicity, biodegradability, and ease of preparation.The physicochemical properties and transformation efficiency of a choline chloride-urea deep eutectic solvent solution were evaluated in this study.Method: The technique of DES synthesis was to blend choline chloride and urea in a 1:2 molar ratio with heat and constant stirring.Physicochemical properties measured were pH, density, viscosity, conductivity, stability and homogeneity.The esterification of ethanol and acetic acid was examined for the organic transformation, and the inorganic application was examined by solubility experiments of copper sulphate.Result: The prepared DES formed a clear, stable, and homogeneous liquid with a pH of 6.4 ± 0.2, density of 1.18 ± 0.03 g/cm³, viscosity of 42.5 ± 2.1 cP, and conductivity of 3.8 ± 0.4 mS/cm.The viscosity decreased with increasing temperature, indicating enhanced molecular mobility.Compared with the conventional aqueous medium, the prepared DES reduced the esterification reaction time from 70 ± 5 min to 35 ± 3 min.In the inorganic application, the DES exhibited improved copper sulphate solubility (96.2 ± 2.1%) and better solution homogeneity than distilled water.Conclusion: Choline chloride-urea DES is a stable, effective and sustainable green solvent with potential uses in organic synthesis, inorganic transformations, and green chemical procedures, according to the study.

The prepared nanoparticles were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency and drug loading. The optimized formulation, F6, showed a particle size of 142.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.218 and a zeta potential of −32.8 mV. Its entrapment efficiency and drug loading were 92.4% and 8.75%, respectively. The optimized nanoparticles were incorporated into a Carbopol 934-based herbal hydrogel containing Aloe vera gel. The optimized hydrogel exhibited a pH of 6.18, viscosity of 18,240 cP, spreadability of 25.3 g·cm/sec, drug content of 98.8% and extrudability of 475 g. In the invitro drug release study, formulation F6 showed 96.4% cumulative drug release over 12 hours, as reported in the study. The release profile fitted the Higuchi model, with an R² value of 0.989. The three-month stability study showed no significant changes in the evaluated formulation parameters under the tested conditions. The findings indicate that the developed SLN-loaded herbal hydrogel has promising formulation characteristics and sustained invitro drug release. Further studies are required to establish its safety, skin penetration and therapeutic effectiveness.
papers.summary: The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate Lopinavir-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) incorporated into a herbal hydrogel for sustained drug delivery. The three-month stability study showed no significant changes in the evaluated formulation parameters under the tested conditions. The findings indicate that the developed SLN-loaded herbal hydrogel has promising formulation characteristics and sustained invitro drug release.

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Nanoemulsion in Combination with Emtricitabine and Tenofovir
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: The therapeutic efficacy of antiretroviral drugs is often limited by poor aqueous solubility, variable bioavailability, and the need for frequent administration. Nanoemulsionbased drug delivery systems offer an attractive strategy to overcome these limitations. Objective: The present study aimed to formulate and optimize an Emtricitabine (FTC) and Tenofovir (TDF) loaded nanoemulsion for enhanced antiretroviral activity. Methods: Solubility studies were performed to select suitable excipients. Capmul MCM was selected as oil, Tween 80 as surfactant, and Transcutol-P as co-surfactant. Pseudo-ternary phase diagrams were constructed, and optimization was performed using a Box-Behnken experimental design. The optimized nanoemulsion was characterized for globule size, PDI, zeta potential, TEM morphology, stability, and in vitro drug release. Results: The optimized formulation exhibited a globule size of 76.8 ± 2.3 nm, PDI of 0.18 ± 0.01, and zeta potential of −39.2 ± 2.1 mV. TEM analysis confirmed spherical droplets with uniform size distribution. The formulation showed excellent thermodynamic stability and sustained drug release with cumulative release of 95.2 ± 4.5% after 24 h. Conclusion: The developed nanoemulsion demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics and controlled release behavior, indicating its potential as a promising carrier system for improved antiretroviral therapy.

papers.title: Nursing Interventions for Reducing Motion-Induced Repeat MRI Sequences in Patients with Cerebrovascular Accident: Causes, Clinical Outcomes, and Multimodal Approaches
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Stillness feels impossible for some inside an MRI tube -movement spoils roughly every fifth scan, grown-ups just as much as children.Machines have gotten sharper over time, yet holding position remains a struggle; appointments stretch longer, costs climb, images blur without warning.Problems come from many directions, not just the person shifting.From 2021 through 2026, studies looked at fixes involving technology tweaks alongside ways to guide patients better.Each year brought small clues on how to reduce blurriness when someone moves too soon.Cerebrovascular accident, commonly known as stroke, is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide.Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone in the diagnosis and management of acute and chronic stroke because of its superior sensitivity in detecting ischemic lesions, hemorrhage, and vascular abnormalities.However, motion-induced artifacts remain a significant challenge during MRI examinations, particularly in patients with CVA who often present with neurological deficits, impaired consciousness, agitation, aphasia, involuntary movements, pain, anxiety, or cognitive dysfunction.Methods: Looking through PubMed, plus EMBASE, along with IEEE Xplore formed the start -adding in unreported studies from company documents and trial logs.Terms like 'MRI motion artifact' mixed with 'deeplearning reconstruction,' then tied to 'radial k-space,' helped narrow things down.'Scanner anxiety,' paired also with 'claustrophobia,' showed up often, just like 'paediatric MRI sedation.'Work from January 2021 into early 2026 got more attention than older reports.Numbers on repeat scans came out next, followed by how long exams took, alongside ratings of nervousness.These pieces grouped together based on shared patterns noticed during sorting.Results: From breathing to heartbeats, body movements stir image blurring.Anxiety or discomfort inside the scanner plays a role too.Instead of straight paths, spinning patterns in data capture handle small shifts better midexam.Systems like GE's AIR Recon DL and Philips' Smart Speed reshape images using smart algorithms.These tools shorten scans by more than a third.Less time means fewer chances for motion to mess things up.When parents stay close or kids practice in pretend scanners beforehand, mistakes drop sharply.In children especially, this cuts retakes nearly one-third.Yet what radiology teams believe often misses current findings on how families actually cope.Gaps linger where science meets daily clinic habits.Conclusion: Getting kids to stay still during scans means mixing fast tech with human care.New imaging cuts wait time, so there's less chance to fidget.Calm coaching before entry helps too, along with having someone familiar nearby.One method on its own won't fix everything.Units using speed upgrades and emotional support together see fewer blurry pictures the first time around.Success sticks when timing and trust run side by side.This review synthesizes current evidence on the causes of motion-induced repeat MRI sequences in patients with cerebrovascular accident, examines their clinical and operational consequences, and highlights evidence-based nursing interventions alongside multimodal technological approaches to improve imaging quality.

papers.title: Mechanical Performance and Compost‐Soil Degradation of Uncompatibilized PLA / PBAT / PCL Blends
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The persistence and fragmentation of conventional petroleum‐based plastics used in agricultural and soil‐contact products have increased the need for biodegradable alternatives that can provide adequate mechanical performance during service while reducing long‐term persistence after disposal. This study investigated uncompatibilized poly(lactic acid) (PLA)/poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT)/poly(ε‐caprolactone) (PCL) binary and ternary blends to evaluate the balance between initial mechanical performance and subsequent degradation under compost‐soil conditions. The PLA content was fixed at 60 wt%, while the relative proportions of PBAT and PCL were varied to determine the influence of blend composition on mechanical, thermal, and degradation behavior. Among the investigated formulations, the ternary blend containing 60 wt% PLA, 20 wt% PBAT, and 20 wt% PCL (P6B2C2) exhibited the most balanced initial mechanical performance. P6B2C2 achieved approximately 73% of the tensile strength and 95% of the tensile modulus of neat PLA without the use of a compatibilizer. DSC analysis revealed distinct component‐specific thermal transitions, confirming the immiscible nature of the blends. The PLA melting temperature remained relatively stable at approximately 148°C–155°C, while PCL retained its characteristic melting peak near 56°C. During 60 days of compost‐soil burial, distinct composition‐dependent degradation responses were observed. The binary PLA/PCL blend (P6C4) exhibited approximately 46% weight loss, accompanied by extensive surface deterioration, cavity formation, and substantial loss of mechanical integrity. In comparison, P6B2C2 exhibited approximately 22% weight loss and retained greater structural integrity throughout the exposure period. SEM observations revealed progressive interfacial deterioration and matrix fragmentation, while FTIR spectra retained the characteristic ester bands without showing substantial formation of new functional groups. The combined weight‐loss, mechanical retention, and physicochemical analyses demonstrate that the degradation response of PLA‐based biodegradable blends can be tailored through blend composition. These findings highlight the potential of ternary PLA/PBAT/PCL blending to balance mechanical performance with soil degradation, providing a material level basis for developing biodegradable alternatives for short life agricultural and soil contact applications.

These findings highlight the potential of ternary PLA/PBAT/PCL blending to balance mechanical performance with soil degradation, providing a material level basis for developing biodegradable alternatives for short life agricultural and soil contact applications.

papers.title: Effect of Ni-additive on jute stick charcoal-mediated carbon anode of Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Li-ion batteries (LIBs) have gained popularity as a potential device for sustainable energy transition. Because of its simple and environmentally benign production, biomass-derived amorphous carbon is a viable anode for LIBs as a possible replacement for graphite. However, its performance is limited by structural deterioration and low conductivity. Therefore, developing low-cost biomass-derived carbon anodes with improved electrical conductivity and cycling stability is important for sustainable LIB applications. Here, slow pyrolysis has been used to produce amorphous carbon from jute stick charcoal. The jute sticks were pyrolyzed at 400 °C, and the structural characterization confirmed the successful formation of amorphous carbon with flake-like porous morphology. The resulting carbon was evaluated as an anode material in a full cell. After 500 cycles, this anode demonstrated a discharge capacity of 125.46 mAh/g and a Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 68.4% at 1C. In addition, Ni metal powder additives were added to improve cell performance. Ni considerably reduced the cell impedance and enhanced electrode conductivity. As a result, after 500 cycles, the Ni-added anode demonstrated improved performance with a discharge capacity of 148.02 mAh/g and a CE of 73% at 1C. Electrochemical investigations further indicated reduced cell resistance after Ni incorporation, demonstrating enhanced electronic conduction and interfacial charge-transfer kinetics.
papers.summary: Therefore, developing low-cost biomass-derived carbon anodes with improved electrical conductivity and cycling stability is important for sustainable LIB applications. The resulting carbon was evaluated as an anode material in a full cell. As a result, after 500 cycles, the Ni-added anode demonstrated improved performance with a discharge capacity of 148.02 mAh/g and a CE of 73% at 1C.

papers.title: Spectroscopic and Thermogravimetric Characterization of Oxidation Products Obtained Using tert-Amyl Chromate as an Oxidant
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The development of efficient and selective oxidizing agents remains an important area of research in organic chemistry. Chromium(VI)-based oxidants have been widely employed for the oxidation of a variety of organic substrates under mild and non-aqueous conditions. However, many conventional chromium oxidants suffer from limitations such as instability, hygroscopic nature, requirement of excess reagent and safety concerns during handling. In the present study, a chromium-based oxidant, tertiary amyl chromate, was synthesized and evaluated for its oxidative behavior toward selected organic substrates. The oxidation products obtained were isolated and characterized using elemental analysis, FTIR spectroscopy and thermogravimetric (TG) analysis. Spectral data confirmed the formation of oxidation products, while thermal studies provided information regarding their stability and decomposition patterns.

papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Resveratrol, a bioactive polyphenolic compound is known to possess potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and anticancer effects, but its clinical use is restricted due to its low aqueous solubility and oral bioavailability.The objective of the present study was to develop and optimize the resveratrol loaded phytosomes with soya lecithin by using rotary evaporation method.The effects of soya lecithin concentration and processing temperature were examined using a 3" factorial design, with respect to particle size and entrapment efficiency.The optimized formulation was subjected to Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) Spectroscopy, Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Particle size analysis, Determination of zeta potential, Drug loading and In vitro drug release study.The optimized formulation (F8) exhibited a particle size of 120.7 ± 0.4 nm, zeta potential of -25.2 ± 1.2 mV, entrapment efficiency of 98.43 ± 1.05%, and drug loading of 98.43 ± 0.46%.FTIR and DSC studies confirmed the formation of a drug-phospholipid complex and the SEM analyses showed the formation of nanosized particles evenly distributed.The optimized phytosomal formulation had 98.85% cumulative drug release while pure resveratrol had 85.76% cumulative drug release.From these results, it can be concluded that phytosomal complexation is an effective method to enhance the physicochemical properties and release behavior of resveratrol with the potential of becoming a good oral delivery system.

papers.title: Formulation Development and Characterization of Benzoyl Peroxide–Emodin Nanostructured Proniosomal Gel for Topical Antifungal Activity against Candida albicans
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The development of localized topical drug delivery systems is of interest for the management of cutaneous fungal infections. This study aimed to develop and characterize a benzoyl peroxide–emodin nanostructured proniosomal gel for topical application and evaluate its in-vitro antifungal activity against Candida albicans. Benzoyl peroxide and emodin proniosomal gels were prepared separately using the coacervation phase separation method with cholesterol, soya lecithin, Span 60, and Tween 80. The optimized formulations were incorporated into Carbopol 934 gel to obtain a combination formulation. The formulations were evaluated for compatibility by FTIR and DSC and characterized for entrapment efficiency, drug content, pH, viscosity, spreadability, vesicle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, surface morphology, and in-vitro drug release. BPPG5 and EmPG5 exhibited the highest entrapment efficiencies of 91.07 ± 1.19% and 85.44 ± 0.63%, respectively, with drug contents of 93.82 ± 0.73% and 90.43 ± 0.81%, respectively. The optimized BPPG5–EmPG5 formulation showed a pH of 6.8 ± 0.93, viscosity of 8639 ± 3.78 cP, and spreadability of 45 ± 1.09 mm. The mean vesicle size, PDI, and zeta potential were 488.1 nm, 0.183, and −32.1 mV, respectively. At 24 h, the cumulative drug release reached 93.21 ± 1.64% for benzoyl peroxide and 90.76 ± 2.19% for emodin. The combination formulation showed a 17 mm zone of inhibition against C. albicans, compared with 16 and 15 mm for BPPG5 and EmPG5, respectively. Overall, the developed formulation exhibited suitable physicochemical characteristics, measurable drug release over 24 h, and promising in-vitro antifungal activity against C. albicans.

papers.title: Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov.: a novel candidate for plant growth-promoting actinomycete from bare soil developing on Miocene lacustrine sediment of the Sokolov Coal Basin, Czech Republic
papers.abstract: Abstract A novel actinomycete, designated as BCCO 10_0861 T , was isolated from overburden Miocene clay sediments undergoing primary succession in Northwest Czechia and characterized by the polyphasic approach. According to 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the strain was closely related to Streptomyces turgidiscabies DSM 41838 T (99.00%), Streptomyces reticuliscabiei DSM 41804 T (98.93%), Streptomyces lacrimifluminis DSM 111125 T (98.15%), and Streptomyces geranii JCM 32177 T (98.08%). Morphological and chemotaxonomic characteristics supported the assignment to the genus Streptomyces . Diagnostic diamino acid in the cell-wall peptidoglycan was LL -diaminopimelic acid and the dominant menaquinone was MK-9(H 6 ). The major cellular fatty acids (> 10%) were anteiso -C 15:0 , iso -C 16:0 , C 16:1 ω7c, and C 16:0 . The polar lipid profile comprised of aminophospholipids, diphosphatidylglycerol, glycophospholipids, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylinositol, and three unidentified phospholipids. The whole cell sugars were galactose, glucose, mannose, ribose, and traces of rhamnose. The genome size of the strain BCCO 10_0861 T was 10.6 Mb with G+C content of 70.05%. Bioinformatic analysis suggested several biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) with medium-to-high similarity confidence to already known BGCs, having ethylenediaminesuccinic acid hydroxyarginine (EDHA), humidimycin, inthomycin B, and triascin C unique to BCCO 10_0861 T . Similarly, predicted plant-growth promoting trait (PGPT) genes differed between genomes, when the one of BCCO 10_0861 T showed the highest number of unique PGPT genes (2,255). In addition, no association with potato pathogenicity was predicted in the genome of BCCO 10_0861 T . The digital DNA-DNA hybridization (ranged from 34.7 to 37.5%), average nucleotide identity values (ranged from 86.26 to 87.24%) and phenotype distinguish strain BCCO 10_0861 T from closely related strains. Based on the polyphasic approach and genomic content, the strain represents a novel species of the genus Streptomyces , for which we propose the name Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov. for BCCO 10_0861 T (= DSM 117345 T ).

papers.title: Study on Quality and Elemental Composition of Gazestan Coal Mine, Takhar Province, Afghanistan
papers.journal: Journal of Mechanical Civil and Industrial Engineering
papers.abstract: Coal is one of the world's main energy resources and has an important role in electricity generation and industrial activities. The chemical and elemental properties of coal are of great importance to its quality and potential uses. In this study, the quality indices and elemental analysis of coal from the Gazestan coal mine in Takhar province in Afghanistan were performed. At approximately 120, 160 and 200 m from the mine entrance, three coal samples were collected at different positions in the coal seam along the second mining gallery. The elemental composition was determined by the XRF analysis and the coal quality indices were evaluated using thermal treatment experiments. The results showed that the sulfur concentrations were in the range of 263-872 ppm with the highest concentration in sample GZ-1. Sample GZ-3 had a calcium concentration of 8.68%, which was much higher than that in other samples. Ash content was found to be between 29.77% and 69.90% whereas volatile matter was found to be between 30.06% and 70.22%. The maximum ash content was observed in sample GZ-2 and the minimum in GZ-3. The results also showed that with the increase in the depth of mining there was a decrease in ash yield and sulfur concentration, along with an increase in calcium content. Such changes can reduce the environmental impacts associated with burning coal. The coal from estimated depth of 200 m was classified as bituminous coal based on quality indices obtained and can be suitable for industrial applications especially in cement manufacturing.

The results showed that the sulfur concentrations were in the range of 263-872 ppm with the highest concentration in sample GZ-1. papers.title: Cement-free composite brick from waste foundry sand and mixed post-consumer thermoplastic waste for sustainable construction
papers.abstract: The emergence of environmentally conscious construction practices aligned with circular economy principles has become increasingly important due to the accelerating depletion of natural resources. Therefore, this study aims to develop a value-added pathway for the reutilisation of waste plastic and foundry sand to create a cement-free perforated composite brick using waste foundry sand (WFS) and mixed post-consumer thermoplastic waste (PTW). The PTW comprised polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), and multilayer plastic (MLP). The WFS, with a fineness modulus of 2.13, was combined with PTW at a 50:50 mass ratio and processed through melt mixing and compression moulding. Ten composite-brick specimens were fabricated and evaluated for their physical and mechanical properties. The developed perforated composite bricks exhibited a water absorption of 1.11% and a mean compressive strength of 5.32 N/mm². Microstructural observations revealed the mechanical encapsulation of WFS particles within a continuous polymer matrix, while the dense packing of the silica-rich WFS contributed to the compact composite structure. This compact structure reduced interconnected voids, resulting in low water absorption. Overall, the developed PTW–WFS composite brick demonstrated good compressive strength and low water absorption, indicating its technical feasibility and potential as a sustainable, environmentally friendly, cement-free alternative for low-load construction applications.
papers.summary: The emergence of environmentally conscious construction practices aligned with circular economy principles has become increasingly important due to the accelerating depletion of natural resources. Therefore, this study aims to develop a value-added pathway for the reutilisation of waste plastic and foundry sand to create a cement-free perforated composite brick using waste foundry sand (WFS) and mixed post-consumer thermoplastic waste (PTW). Overall, the developed PTW–WFS composite brick demonstrated good compressive strength and low water absorption, indicating its technical feasibility and potential as a sustainable, environmentally friendly, cement-free alternative for low-load construction applications.

papers.title: Tech Mining with LLMs: Unveiling Trends from Corporate Websites
papers.abstract: Abstract Technology mining enables the systematic extraction and analysis of trends regarding scientific and technological developments from diverse Science, Technology, and Innovation (ST&I) data sources. Traditionally, indicators such as patents, surveys, and R&D statistics have been widely used to monitor technological change and innovation. This study proposes a novel methodology leveraging semantic analysis of corporate website content using large language models (LLMs) to facilitate real-time monitoring of technological developments. Specifically, we focus on Spanish manufacturing firms that have adopted artificial intelligence (AI). A pipeline was developed to automatically extract and classify bigrams and unigrams from corporate websites into technological and non-technological terms, enabling a temporal analysis of technologies for the years 2023 and 2025. The results indicate an increase in AI-related mentions, as well as notable patterns of co-occurrence with Internet of Things (IoT) and Industry 4.0 technologies. Our study demonstrates the utility of the combination of corporate websites and LLMs as scalable, dynamic, and cost-effective sources for technology mining, contributing methodologically through advanced text analytics and empirically by providing granular, web-derived insights into technological dynamics within the manufacturing sector.

papers.title: A chemically etched D-band waveguide orthomode transducer for CMB measurements
papers.abstract: Abstract This study presents a prototype D-band waveguide orthomode transducer (OMT) fabricated using chemically etched brass platelets. This method offers a fast, cost-effective, and scalable approach for producing such devices above 100 GHz, making it well-suited for current and future Cosmic Microwave Background polarization experiments, where large focal planes with thousands of receivers are required to detect the faint primordial B -modes. Chemical etching has already demonstrated its effectiveness in manufacturing corrugated feedhorn arrays with state-of-the-art performance up to 150 GHz. Here, we evaluate its applicability to more complex structures, such as OMTs. We designed a single OMT prototype operating in the 130–170 GHz range, fabricated by chemically etching 0.15 mm-thick brass plates, which were then stacked, aligned, and mechanically clamped. Simulations based on metrological measurements of the OMT profile predict reflected power below −10 dB, cross-polarization better than −30 dB, and transmission around −0.5 dB in the 140−170 GHz band. Measurements yield transmisison around −1.5/−2 dB and cross-polarization $$<-$$ 20 dB. Further simulations show that the degradation in the transmission is related to defects and roughness along the etched profile ( $$\textrm{RMS}\simeq $$ 3 $$\mu $$ m), which is a typical and unavoidable effect of chemical etching. The discrepancy in cross-polarization, instead, could arise from a $$\sim $$ 1.5 $$^{\circ }$$ rotation of the polarization angle within the measurement chain. Our results show that chemical etching is a fast, low-cost, and scalable technique for producing waveguide OMTs with state-of-the-art performance in terms of reflected power and cross-polarization. However, at frequencies above 100 GHz our results show that the mechanical precision limitations of the chemical etching process degrade the transmission coefficient.

papers.title: Halogen‐Driven Trade‐Off Between Humidity and Thermal Stability in Zero‐Dimensional Hybrid Manganese Halides for Dual‐Stimulus Encryption
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Zero‐dimensional (0D) hybrid manganese halides are attractive lead‐free luminescent materials, yet the simultaneous demands for moisture and thermal stability pose a fundamental challenge. Here we demonstrate a halogen‐driven trade‐off between humidity and thermal stability in (BrPhTMN) 2 MnX 4 (X = Cl, Br, I) with a non‐hydrogen‐bonding cation. Replacing Cl with I dramatically increases the photoluminescence quantum yield (from 20.2% to 84.3%) but drastically reduces humidity resistance at 90% relative humidity (RH) (from ∼51 h for the bromide to <14 min for the iodide). Remarkably, the thermal stability trend is reversed: the iodide shows enhanced emission at 430 K, whereas the chloride is heavily quenched. This paradoxical thermal robustness of the iodide, despite its large electron–phonon coupling (Huang–Rhys factor S = 4.43), can be rationalized by the energy‐gap law for multiphonon relaxation. Raman spectroscopy reveals an exceptionally low Mn–I phonon frequency (111 cm −1 ), which exponentially suppresses multiphonon non‐radiative decay, effectively closing the non‐radiative channel even under strong coupling. Exploiting these orthogonal stabilities, we construct a dual‐stimulus encryption device responsive to specific humidity‐heat sequences. This work establishes a design principle for anti‐thermal‐quenching luminescent materials and opens avenues for advanced stimulus‐responsive systems.

papers.title: Nonclinical Toxicology and Immunogenicity Strategy for AAV-Based Gene Therapies in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: An IND-Enabling Case Analysis
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector gene therapies deliver a functional or partially functional transgene to treat genetic disease through a single, typically intravenous, administration, and represent a mechanistically distinct category from both small-molecule and conventional biologic therapeutics. At least one AAV-based micro-dystrophin gene therapy has received regulatory approval for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, establishing a labelled risk profile, including acute liver injury, myocarditis, immune-mediated myositis, and thrombotic microangiopathy, that directly shapes nonclinical safety assessment for this product category. This article develops a complete, IND-enabling nonclinical toxicology and immunogenicity strategy for AAV-based gene therapies in this indication, built on FDA guidance for cellular and gene therapy products, gene therapy products incorporating a disease-relevant animal model, shedding and biodistribution assessment, and long-term follow-up. The package integrates test-article supply planning expressed in vector genomes per kilogram, a dual-rodent-model design using both a disease-relevant strain and a wild-type comparator, a non-human-primate pivotal safety study with cardiovascular telemetry and recovery, a comprehensive immunogenicity and toxicokinetic assessment program, biodistribution and shedding studies addressing environmental release and germline risk, and a waiver-rationale approach to classical reproductive and genotoxicity testing appropriate for a non-integrating viral vector. Beyond the specific case, the article develops general principles for translating labelled clinical risks directly into nonclinical safety endpoints, and closes with recommendations for the nonclinical section of an IND application for this drug category. Keywords: AAV gene therapy; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; micro-dystrophin; immunogenicity; biodistribution; shedding; IND application; FDA gene therapy guidance

papers.title: Interfacially Regulated MXene‐Based Nanocomposite Membranes for Highly Selective Ion Transport and Salinity Gradient Energy Harvesting
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid (HA) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties. The optimized membrane achieved near‐ideal monovalent cation selectivity (∼99%), a low area‐specific membrane resistance of 0.06 Ω·m 2 , and an energy conversion efficiency of 45.6%. The same membrane was evaluated over multiple electrochemical testing cycles totaling approximately 300 h, including dedicated 48 h stability measurements under heavy‐metal‐ and organic‐foulant‐containing conditions. A model‐based assessment of a conceptual reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack predicts a 37% increase in power generation, accompanied by an increase in energy conversion efficiency from 30.0% to 41.1%, relative to the commercial‐membrane scenario. These findings demonstrate that regulating interfacial interactions provides an effective design strategy for developing MXene‐based ion‐selective membranes for salinity‐gradient energy harvesting and related electrochemical separation processes.

papers.title: Effect of Glutathione S‐Transferase and Metallothionein Polymorphisms on Mercury Levels and End‐Stage Renal Disease ( ESRD ) in Colombian Patients
papers.abstract: Epidemiological studies have demonstrated a link between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and environmental mercury (Hg) exposure. Colombia has a well-documented history of artisanal and small-scale gold mining, where Hg exposure affects miners and nearby riverside and urban populations. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of polymorphisms in GSTM1, GSTT1, MT1A (rs8052394), and MT2A (rs10636) on Hg levels and their relationship with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in a Colombian urban population. We conducted a cross-sectional, multicenter exploratory study on 401 CKD patients to assess the impact of polymorphisms on total Hg (tHg) levels in blood and hair, and their relationship with ESRD. Patients were divided into two groups: Group 1 (G1) with patients in Stages 1-4 CKD, and Group 2 (G2) with patients in Stage 5 CKD. Unexpectedly, tHg levels were low in our population (GM (SD) = 0.69 (2.07) and 0.73 (2.18) μg/L in blood, and GM (SD) = 0.22 (3.80) and 0.18 (2.9) μg/g in hair for G1 and G2, respectively). We found that low hair tHg levels were significantly associated with null GSTT1, double null GSTM1/GSTT1, and MT1A (rs8052394) GG genotype in G1, and high tHg with the null GSTM1 genotype in G2 patients. Furthermore, when pooling G1 and G2, the double-null genotype of GSTM1/GSTT1, as well as MT1A (rs8052394) AA and MT2A (rs10636) GC, were more prevalent among patients with hair and blood tHg levels exceeding 1 μg/g and 5 μg/L, respectively. Patients carrying the MT1A (rs8052394) AG genotype exhibited an increased risk of ESRD. In conclusion, our findings suggest that, even in a population with low Hg exposure, polymorphisms in glutathione S-transferases and metallothioneins showed stage-specific associations with hair tHg levels, and that MT1A may contribute to ESRD risk.

papers.title: Multiple dimensions of taxonomic tree diversity reveal complementary effects of environmental filtering and land-use legacy in an urban Atlantic Forest
papers.abstract: Abstract The Brazilian Atlantic Forest is a highly diverse ecosystem that has been extensively fragmented by human activities, making secondary urban forests important for biodiversity conservation. However, the influence of environmental filtering and land-use legacies on taxonomic diversity during forest regeneration remains poorly understood. We evaluated tree community diversity along environmental gradients under contrasting management histories in an urban secondary forest in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. Three regenerating communities with a common origin as shaded coffee agroforestry systems were sampled: second-growth forest after silvicultural management (SGAM), second-growth forest after enrichment with Euterpe edulis (SGAE), and second-growth forest under natural regeneration (SGA). Phytosociological, topographic, soil, and litter data were analyzed using Hill numbers (q = 0, 1, 2) through iNEXT.3D and iNEXT.beta3D, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS), and Generalized Linear Mixed Models. PCA revealed edaphic and elevation gradients, whereas NMDS showed significant differences in species composition. Species richness (q = 0) was highest in SGAE and SGA, while dominance-weighted diversity (q = 1 and 2) was greater in SGAE and SGAM. Species richness increased with elevation, effective cation exchange capacity, sand content, and litter carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, but decreased with clay content, whereas management history showed little influence. In contrast, abundance-weighted diversity was primarily driven by management history, but also increased with litter carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and elevation. These findings indicate that environmental filtering shapes species richness, whereas land-use legacies have persistent effects on community structure, highlighting the importance of multidimensional approaches for evaluating and restoring secondary urban tropical forests.

papers.title: Cryogenic minimum quantity lubrication for improving the surface integrity of AISI 347
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Metastable austenitic steels exhibit a unique hardening mechanism based on a strain-induced phase transformation from ductile austenite to hard martensite, which can be triggered by high plastic deformation at low temperatures. In previous studies, this transformation was successfully promoted during turning by applying large amounts of CO₂. However, the associated high consumption of coolant limits the economic feasibility of this approach. This study introduces a hybrid cooling and lubrication strategy combining CO₂ with minimum quantity lubrication (cMQL). Both media are supplied in very small quantities (0.1–0.2 kg/min CO₂ and 2.60 g/h oil). Two oils specifically developed for use at cryogenic conditions were investigated and compared to pure CO₂ cooling and dry cutting. The objective was to achieve deformation-induced martensite formation while significantly reducing CO₂ consumption. The results demonstrate that the hybrid cMQL approach enables the generation of smooth surfaces together with moderate martensitic transformation. The findings highlight the potential of cryogenic MQL as a resource-efficient alternative to conventional cryogenic cooling for improving surface integrity in the machining of metastable austenitic steels.

papers.title: Design and testing of kinematic electromagnetic induction heating system for manufacturing of high-performance carbon fiber composites
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: The present paper reports development of a novel concept of electromagnetic induction heating system for manufacturing of high-performance carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites. The proposed induction heating system consists of several key parts such as medium-to-high frequency generator, induction coil with 3 degrees of freedom movement controlled by a CNC software, high-resolution thermal imaging camera with live workpiece temperature distribution data processing algorithm. The proposed system allows for mitigation of highly non-uniform temperature distribution associated with induction heating such as formation of cold spots, skin and corner effects, which are further amplified due to high material anisotropy of CFRPs caused by difference in mechanical and physical properties in longitudinal and transverse direction of the fibers. In the present work, movement of the induction coil during induction heating was set to simple cyclic rectangular paths which resulted in a more uniform temperature distribution and a significantly larger area of composite subjected to sufficient curing temperature compared to static coil systems. Efficiency of induction curing of the designed system was evaluated by experimental measurement of temperature distribution in dry fabrics and pre-preg laminates. Validation of induction heating system efficiency was performed by mechanical and degree-of-cure experimental tests of different configurations of carbon/epoxy prepreg laminates. Additionally, challenges in air void entrapment in the material due to non-uniform distribution of soft and solid resin regions during the curing process were encountered and potential mechanisms of their entrapment were analyzed.

papers.title: Optimization and mechanistic analysis of high-temperature aerobic composting process for dynamic sludge in rotary drums
papers.abstract: This study addresses challenges in high-temperature aerobic sludge composting using a rotary drum, particularly material adhesion to the drum wall and low efficiency. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to develop predictive models for composting period time and seed germination index (GI). The models showed high reliability (R²≥ 0.95, p < 0.001) with validation errors of 6.67% for composting period and 1.04% for GI. The optimal conditions identified were 55% moisture content, 10 mm auxiliary material dimensions, 7 L·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ TS aeration rate, and 1.5 r·min⁻¹ rotational speed. These conditions reduced the composting period to 15 days, increased GI to 86%, and met the GB/T 23,486 − 2009 standards for heavy metal concentrations. The bioavailability of heavy metals decreased significantly, ensuring environmental safety. Microbial community analysis revealed a two-stage succession pattern, with thermophilic Bacillus and Aspergillus dominating the high-temperature phase. The process efficiency was influenced by synergistic parameter interactions. Through comparative analysis of processes, it was found that rotating drum composting achieves an optimal balance among efficiency, environmental performance, and engineering feasibility, making it highly suitable for large-scale municipal sludge valorization.

papers.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
papers.journal: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. papers.title: Meso-NH-ISO v1.0: a water stable isotopologue scheme in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH – application to a 2D West African squall line
papers.abstract: Abstract. Better understanding how convective processes impact the isotopic composition of atmospheric water has implications for understanding present-day phenomena such as squall lines or tropical cyclones, and for reconstructions of past rainfall extreme events. With this motivation, we implemented water stable isotopes in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH. Water stable isotopes are implemented in the advection of water phases and in the microphysical scheme. The implementation is validated on a test case of a 2D simulation of a tropical squall line observed in June 1981 during the COPT81 field campaign in the Sahel region. The isotopic version of Meso-NH (Meso-NH-ISO) captures the expected evolution of the isotopic composition of both precipitation and water vapor along the squall line. This work opens the door to future isotopic studies using realistic cases of mesoscale convective systems (squall lines, tropical cyclones).

papers.title: Application of LHC gas recuperation systems for methane emission control in livestock housing
papers.abstract: Abstract The CH4rLiE (CH4 Livestock Emission) project presents a dry-gas laboratory proof-of-principle for mitigating methane (CH4) emissions in livestock housing. This work investigates the technical feasibility of capturing CH4 at low concentrations by adapting gas recovery systems originally developed for Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments at CERN. A laboratory-scale prototype was evaluated using dry synthetic gas mixtures across 899-4509 ppm, leading to the selection of commercial Z5 zeolite as the primary adsorbent due to its higher capacity compared to the other materials tested and stable Vacuum Swing Adsorption (VSA) regeneration performance. To bridge the gap to representative dairy barn conditions (10-100 ppm) where direct experimental validation was not conducted, thermodynamic models (Toth, Langmuir, Henry) were used to extrapolate adsorption behavior down to 50 ppm. Consequently, adsorbent mass requirements in the ultra-low concentration regime represent preliminary model projections rather than direct empirical measurements. These results validate the operational concept and provide foundational parameters for full-scale field prototype development.

papers.title: High-fidelity 3D geometric reconstruction of pelvic organs from MRI: a hybrid deep learning and iterative optimization approach
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective. The generation of high-fidelity, high-quality three-dimensional (3D) pelvic organ geometries from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived segmentation masks remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid framework for reconstructing the bladder, uterus, and rectum, and to assess its geometric fidelity, mesh-quality proxy performance, and reconstruction efficiency. Approach. We developed a hybrid deformable shape modeling framework that integrates deep learning prediction with iterative optimization for the reconstruction of the bladder, uterus, and rectum. The framework consists of three core components: (1) a geometry-aware multi-level deep learning architecture that preserves topological consistency of pelvic organs; (2) a two-stage amortized optimization training strategy that balances global shape capture and local surface refinement; and (3) a holistic synergy mechanism—where iterative optimization provides supervision for deep learning during the training phase, and during inference, deep learning rapidly predicts the global organ morphology, followed by iterative optimization to refine local surfaces and mesh quality. Main results. Before iterative refinement, the proposed model outperformed representative deep learning-based reconstruction methods in geometric fidelity, achieving CD/DSC values of 5.5 × 10⁻³/0.788 for the bladder, 3.7 × 10⁻³/0.839 for the rectum, and 4.2 × 10⁻³/0.900 for the uterus. Deep learning-based initialization enabled the complete hybrid framework to converge within approximately 100 iterations, with a reconstruction time of approximately 35 s per organ on a CPU and 1.5 s on a GPU. At the patient level, the mean minSICN and minSIGE values of the 10 worst volumetric elements were 0.0807 and 0.0844, respectively, exceeding those achieved by traditional geometric post-processing methods. Significance. The proposed framework connects image-domain segmentation with structural-domain applications by efficiently generating high-fidelity, high-quality pelvic organ geometries with improved mesh-quality proxy performance. These geometries may support statistical shape assessment and may provide candidate surface representations for subsequent volumetric meshing and solver-specific biomechanical validation.
