papers.title: MAOMAO: an ontology-guided FAIR resource for harmonized peptide toxicity data
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides have emerged as a rapidly expanding class of biomolecules with applications spanning antimicrobial, antiviral, anticancer, immunomodulatory, metabolic, and diagnostic settings (8). Their high target specificity, favorable safety profiles, and growing clinical success have positioned them as attractive alternatives or complements to traditional small-molecule therapeutics (36). The number of experimentally characterized bioactive peptides has therefore increased substantially during the last decade (38), supporting the development of specialized databases and computational resources for peptide discovery, functional annotation, and rational design (5,15,31,35). Despite these advances, toxicity remains a major limitation to peptide development and clinical translation, constraining candidate selection during early-stage screening and optimization (3).Peptide toxicity encompasses a broad spectrum of adverse biological effects that arise from the interaction between peptides and biological systems. Most toxicity phenotypes are routinely evaluated during peptide development including cytotoxicity, hemolysis, neurotoxicity, embryotoxicity, and ichthyotoxicity (19,27). These toxicity endpoints have direct implications for efficacy, safety, dosage, and regulatory approval. Toxicity annotations have consequently accumulated across public databases (31,18,24), literature-derived resources (26,29,28,34), supplementary datasets (9,4,23), and experimental studies (33,39). However, these resources remain fragmented, employ heterogeneous terminology and annotation criteria, and provide variable levels of metadata and evidence quality (21). Their development for distinct biological objectives further complicates integration, reproducibility, and large-scale analysis (17).The growing availability of toxicity data creates opportunities for computational toxicology, data-driven peptide engineering, and large-scale biological analyses (32). Their utility, however, depends on the quality, consistency, and transparency of the underlying data (14,7). Annotation ambiguity, conflicting evidence, heterogeneous endpoint definitions, incomplete metadata, and limited provenance tracking can reduce reproducibility and complicate downstream reuse (1). The FAIR principles-Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability-provide a framework for organizing and distributing scientific data to support discovery, integration, reproducibility, and long-term reuse (22). Nevertheless, a standardized framework that harmonizes heterogeneous peptidetoxicity annotations while preserving evidence, provenance, and metadata remains largely unavailable (21). FAIR-oriented resources tailored to both biological interpretation and computational reuse are therefore still needed (37,13).To address these limitations, we developed MAOMAO (Metadata-Aware Ontology for Multi-source Annotation Organization), an ontology-guided resource integrating peptide-toxicity information from public databases, literature-derived resources, and curated datasets. MAOMAO standardizes toxicity terminology, preserves source-level provenance, distinguishes uncertainty-related evidence states, and organizes annotations within a unified hierarchical framework. The resource also provides harmonized metadata, descriptor-based representations, protein language model embeddings, benchmark resources, and supporting documentation. These components establish a FAIR-oriented and reusable foundation for biological interpretation, computational toxicology, and predictive modeling of peptide toxicity.The workflow used to construct MAOMAO is summarized in Figure 1A. Toxicity-related information from heterogeneous sources was preprocessed, harmonized, mapped to a unified toxicity ontology, evaluated for annotation conflicts and evidence quality, enriched with standardized metadata, and consolidated into the final resource. To support dissemination, computational reuse, and long-term maintenance, MAOMAO was organized into a modular architecture comprising complementary resource layers (Figure 1B).MAOMAO was constructed by integrating toxicity-related information from publicly available databases, literature-derived resources, supplementary datasets, and manually curated repositories. Candidate resources were identified through a structured exploration of the peptide toxicity landscape using scientific search engines, bibliographic repositories, specialized peptide databases, review articles, and citation tracking (2,16). Searches combined general terms, including peptide toxicity, toxic peptides, toxic peptide databases, and toxic peptide predictive models, with endpoint-specific queries for hemolytic peptides, cytotoxic peptides, cytolytic peptides, neurotoxic peptides, embryotoxic peptides, ichthyotoxic peptides, and anti mammalian cells peptides. Additional resources were identified from toxicity prediction tools, benchmark datasets, supplementary materials, associated repositories, and specialized peptide resources. Searches were conducted using Google Scholar and PubMed (6) between June 2025 and September 2026 and covered resources available through September 2026.Candidate resources were evaluated according to predefined eligibility criteria, including relevance to at least one MAOMAO toxicity endpoint, availability of peptide sequences with corresponding categorical toxicity annotations or quantitative toxicity measurements, sufficient provenance information, and the possibility of programmatic or manual retrieval. Resources were excluded when the underlying dataset could not be retrieved through the reported publication, supplementary material, repository, or web server, or when the available material lacked sequences suitable for sequence-level integration. This included resources containing only numerical representations, peptide names, or functional annotations without the corresponding sequences. Candidate-source screening, eligibility decisions, integrated and excluded resources, and source-specific exclusion reasons are detailed in Supplementary Section S1. (A) Ontology-guided harmonization workflow used to construct the resource. Toxicity-related information collected from public databases, literature-derived datasets, and curated resources undergoes preprocessing, terminology harmonization, ontology mapping, evidence integration, quantitative-property parsing, and metadata harmonization to generate a standardized and provenance-aware toxicity resource. (B) Modular architecture of MAOMAO. The resource is organized into complementary layers comprising harmonized toxicity annotations, numerical toxicity properties, sequence profiles, and metadata (Core Layer), sequence-derived descriptors (Descriptor Layer), protein language model embeddings (Embedding Layer), benchmark resources (Benchmark Layer), practical usage examples, and supporting documentation (Documentation Layer). Together, these components establish a FAIR-oriented and reusable resource for peptide toxicity research.Data acquisition combined direct database downloads, repository and supplementary-file retrieval, and manual extraction when required. Retrieved records were converted into a standardized intermediate representation, preserving peptide sequences, toxicity annotations, quantitative toxicity measurements when available, source identifiers, literature references, and available metadata. Source-level quality control verified the reported access route, the availability of primary sequences and interpretable toxicity information, and the associated publication or repository. Records lacking peptide sequences, containing toxicity information that could not be interpreted, or presenting irrecoverable formatting inconsistencies were excluded. Retained records were then forwarded to preprocessing, terminology harmonization, ontology mapping, metadata harmonization, and evidence integration.Following data collection, records underwent standardized preprocessing to support integration across heterogeneous resources (Figure 1A). This stage included sequence validation, format standardization, annotation parsing, identifier normalization, and quality control. The final resource was restricted to peptides containing the 20 canonical amino acids and lengths between 5 and 70 residues (38,25). Recoverable formatting inconsistencies were corrected, exact duplicates within each source were removed, and identical sequences reported by different sources were retained to preserve provenance and support evidence integration. Each normalized sequence was assigned a deterministic identifier generated by applying SHA-256 to the UTF-8 encoding of the uppercase, whitespace-free sequence. Quantitative HC50, LC50, LD50, and MHC observations were parsed while preserving their reported relation, value, unit, and provenance, and were linked to Core sequences through this identifier. Detailed sequence-processing, identifier-construction, and quantitative-property procedures are provided in Supplementary Section S1.To prevent terminology inconsistencies during cross-source integration, toxicity-related annotations were examined for alternative spellings, synonyms, endpoint-specific descriptions, and sourcedependent nomenclature referring to equivalent biological concepts. These variants were mapped to a standardized vocabulary while preserving their original biological meaning. For example, haemolytic was normalized to hemolytic, and cytolytic to cytolysis.Harmonized annotations were mapped to the MAOMAO toxicity ontology, centered on the root category Toxic. The ontology comprises Cytotoxic, Neurotoxic, Embryotoxic, and Ichthyotoxic as primary classes, with Hemolytic, Cytolysis, and Anti mammalian cells represented as subclasses of Cytotoxic. Hemolytic denotes toxicity involving erythrocyte lysis, whereas Cytolysis captures cell lysis or membrane-disruptive activity without a specified cell type. Anti-mammalian-cell activity denotes damage to mammalian cells or reduced cell viability (20,30,40). The vocabulary was restricted to distinct toxicity concepts supported by retrievable sequence-level evidence. Complete endpoint definitions, mappings, and assignment rules are provided in Supplementary Section S2.Following data collection, harmonization, and ontology mapping, annotations associated with identical peptide sequences were aggregated across sources (Figure 1A). Because the same sequence could be reported with different toxicity annotations, an evidence-management framework was applied to classify each peptide-endpoint pair as positive, negative, ambiguous, unlabeled, or no information. Positive states represented direct or hierarchy-supported toxicity evidence, whereas negative states corresponded to direct endpoint-specific non-toxic evidence. Ambiguous states captured conflicting or unresolved annotations. Unlabeled states denoted sequences retained in endpoint-specific sources without an explicit class assignment, while no information indicated the absence of evidence for that endpoint.Negative evidence was further classified as strong or weak according to the supporting information available in the original source. Strong negatives were explicitly supported by experimental evidence, whereas weak negatives originated from randomly selected negative sets or lacked confirmation of the absence of toxicity annotations. Evidence strength was retained in the metadata and provenance records, enabling downstream analyses to account for confidence, uncertainty, and conflicting evidence. Definitions, assignment criteria, and conflict-resolution rules are provided in Supplementary Section S2.To support transparency, interoperability, and long-term reuse, source-and endpoint-level metadata were normalized into a unified schema. Harmonized fields included source identifiers, literature references, organism information, annotation provenance, retrieval dates, file formats, and version information when available. Missing values were explicitly preserved without inference. The schema also retained original source labels, ontology mappings, evidence categories, publication references, and resource-specific annotations, providing a standardized representation of the integrated biological and technical information.Provenance was maintained by linking harmonized annotations to their source-specific processed datasets, endpoint-integration outputs, and metadata records. The sequence-level pivot provides the harmonized access layer, while provenance records, the ambiguity-support table, and the hierarchyaudit table document evidence aggregation, conflict resolution, and hierarchy-derived changes. These files allow each sequence-endpoint state to be traced to its supporting sources and processing decisions. Metadata fields, controlled vocabularies, and data types are detailed in Supplementary Section S3.To support reproducibility, computational reuse, and long-term maintenance, MAOMAO was organized into complementary functional layers (Figure 1B). This modular architecture separates harmonized biological data, computational representations, benchmark resources, and supporting documentation while preserving interoperability across the resource.The Core Layer contains harmonized peptide sequences, toxicity annotations, ontology mappings, evidence classifications, provenance information, and metadata. It additionally provides numerical toxicity properties and sequence profiles. Descriptor-based representations were generated using Roxy (11), whereas embedding-based representations were obtained with Sylphy (12) using publicly available protein language models. Benchmark resources were generated using partitioning strategies implemented through BioSieve (10). The Documentation Layer contains ontology specifications, metadata schemas, resource descriptions, licensing information, and versioning records. Supported representations, benchmark resources, resource organization, and file structures are detailed in Supplementary Sections S4-S5.FAIR principles guided the design and construction of MAOMAO to support transparency, reproducibility, interoperability, and long-term sustainability. FAIR-oriented practices were incorporated across data collection, terminology harmonization, ontology development, evidence management, metadata integration, and resource organization.Interoperability and reusability were supported through standardized toxicity terminology, ontology-guided endpoint mapping, harmonized metadata schemas, explicit evidence categorization, provenance tracking, and version-aware organization. These components enable heterogeneous toxicity annotations to be integrated while preserving the original information associated with each record.Findability, accessibility, and computational reuse were supported by distributing resource components in machine-readable formats and using standardized identifiers linking sequences, annotations, metadata, ontology terms, and evidence categories. The sequence-derived SHA-256 identifiers provide a stable key for linking corresponding records across the Core, Descriptor, Embedding, Benchmark, and sequence-profile resources. Harmonization procedures, ontology definitions, evidence-management rules, metadata specifications, and generation workflows were also documented to support validation, updates, and downstream use. Resource availability, file organization, versioning, and supporting documentation are detailed in Supplementary Section S5.An overview of MAOMAO is presented in Figure 2A. The resource integrates toxicity-related information from 56 publicly available databases, literature-derived resources, supplementary datasets, and manually curated repositories. Of 1,372,190 non-deduplicated source-level records initially collected, 898,637 were retained after source-specific preprocessing, representing a reduction of approximately 34.5%. Removed records included duplicates, incomplete entries, formatting inconsistencies, and annotations that did not satisfy the inclusion criteria.Following terminology harmonization, ontology mapping, cross-source evidence aggregation, state resolution, and quality control, the final release comprised 71,857 unique peptide sequences across eight toxicity-related endpoints. These were organized into 574,856 sequence-endpoint combinations, together with standardized metadata and provenance records linking annotations, ontology assignments, evidence classifications, and source-specific information.Publication references, repository or server information, download dates, file formats, source types, and resource behavior were documented for all 56 sources. Annotation content and last-update dates were available for 55 sources (98.21%), whereas explicit licensing information was available for 15 sources (26.79%). Missing metadata were preserved without inference. These components provide a harmonized resource for organizing, disseminating, and computationally analyzing peptide toxicity information.The ontology-guided organization of toxicity annotations is presented in Figure 2B. The root category Toxic contains 57,080 available peptide-endpoint states, including 13,824 positives, and comprises four primary classes, namely Cytotoxic (25,454 available states; 7,122 positive), Neurotoxic (3,183; 1,481 positive), Embryotoxic (2 positive), and Ichthyotoxic (5 positive). The Cytotoxic branch is further divided into Hemolytic (35,960 available states; 4,714 positive), Cytolysis (343; 341 positive), and Anti mammalian cells (21,393 available states; 3,664 positive), preserving more specific biological contexts. These categories define the endpoint structure used throughout MAOMAO.Evidence-state distributions are summarized in Figure 2C and Supplementary Table S10. Across MAOMAO, 31,153 states were positive, 91,506 negative, 15,717 ambiguous, and 5,044 unlabeled. Because only positive annotations were propagated through the hierarchy, all other states remained endpoint-specific, and no-information states were excluded from the percentages shown in Figure 2C. Toxic contained 13,824 positives, whereas Hemolytic had the highest proportion of ambiguous states (19.05%) and was the only endpoint with unlabeled states, representing 14.03% of its available annotations.Across the seven non-root endpoints, 7,331 of the 9,421 peptides with at least one positive annotation were assigned to multiple toxicity categories. This corresponds to 77.82% of positive peptides across these endpoints and 10.2% of all MAOMAO sequences. Percentages were calculated relative to the positive sequences assigned to each row endpoint and should therefore be interpreted directionally. The largest overlap occurred between Cytotoxic and Hemolytic, with 4,128 shared sequences, representing 57.96% of cytotoxic-positive and 87.57% of hemolytic-positive sequences. Complete pairwise counts and directional percentages are provided in Supplementary Section S2.MAOMAO distributes harmonized annotations, numerical representations, benchmark resources, metadata, ontology definitions, and documentation across the functional layers shown in Figure 1B.The Core Layer contains 574,856 harmonized peptide-endpoint combinations corresponding to 71,857 unique sequences, together with ontology assignments, evidence classifications, provenance, and standardized metadata. It additionally provides 169 HC50, LC50, LD50, and MHC measurement records. Most were linked to the Core sequence universe, while six LD50 records remained unmatched because their sequences exceeded the 70-residue limit. One profile per Core sequence summarizes its activity annotations, supporting evidence, ontology effects, toxicity targets, selected descriptors, and available numerical toxicity properties. The Descriptor Layer provides 41 features capturing sequence composition and physicochemical properties.The Embedding Layer includes 10 protein-language-model embedding matrices and a one-hot representation, all covering the complete set of 71,857 MAOMAO sequences.The Benchmark Layer contains 300 endpoint-seed-strategy configurations generated through random and stratified five-fold partitioning of five eligible endpoints (Toxic, Cytotoxic, Hemolytic, Neurotoxic, and Anti mammalian cells) using 30 random seeds. These correspond to 1,500 data partitions and, across the 11 numerical representations, 3,300 representation-specific configurations and 16,500 fold instances. Associated parameters, reports, summaries, and execution records are also provided.The Documentation Layer includes ontology definitions, metadata schemas, resource descriptions, versioning records, and licensing information. Files are distributed in standard formats, including CSV, JSON, and YAML, with detailed component descriptions and inventories provided in Supplementary Sections S4-S5.To facilitate direct reuse of the distributed assets, MAOMAO provides five executable notebooks that operate on the released files rather than reconstructing the resource from the original sources. The introductory workflow covers resource access, file validation, navigation of the Core Layer, and linkage of annotations, numerical representations, and benchmark partitions through stable sequence identifiers. Complementary notebooks support descriptive characterization of endpoint states, class balance, co-occurrence, sequence lengths, ontology consistency, and representation coverage, as well as retrieval and querying of individual sequence profiles. Generated tables and figures are stored separately from the released resource files.Two additional notebooks illustrate downstream machine-learning reuse. The neurotoxicity classification example joins a released train-validation-test partition with an existing protein language model representation and evaluates logistic regression, a linear support vector machine, and random forest models using fixed settings. The quantitative regression example shows how MAOMAO's numerical toxicity measurements can be combined with a released sequence representation in a simple regression analysis. These workflows are intended to demonstrate resource interoperability and reproducible reuse rather than establish state-of-the-art predictors or replace the released benchmark design. Detailed descriptions of the demonstration notebooks, execution requirements, and generated outputs are provided in Supplementary Section S6MAOMAO was designed as a reusable resource for peptide toxicity research, providing a harmonized collection of toxicity annotations, ontology mappings, evidence classifications, metadata records, numerical representations, and benchmark resources. papers.title: The Closer, the Better: Engineering RGB Thermometric Performance in Tb3+,Eu3+-Doped MOFs
papers.abstract: Abstract The effectiveness of luminescence thermometry, which exploits temperature-induced changes in the spectroscopic properties of phosphor materials for temperature sensing, has been extensively demonstrated. However, from a practical perspective, monitoring temperature-induced variations in the color of the emitted light offers a considerably more straightforward and user-friendly alternative to conventional spectral analysis. In this context, establishing a clear relationship between the thermal evolution of the emission color and the structure of the phosphor is essential for the rational design of visual luminescence thermometers. In this work, we investigate the correlation between the temperature-dependent emission color and the structural characteristics of Tb3+,Eu3+-co-doped metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), with particular emphasis on their potential for filter-free, camera-based thermal sensing. The obtained results demonstrate that, within the investigated series of materials, decreasing the interionic distance between Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions increases the probability of energy transfer and consequently enhances the thermal sensitivity of the camera-based readout derived from the ratio of luminescence intensities recorded in the blue and red channels. These findings establish a direct relationship between the structural characteristics of the luminescent material, the underlying energy-transfer processes, and its thermometric performance. More broadly, this study provides a foundation for the rational design of visual luminescence thermometers with predefined sensing characteristics, opening a pathway toward structure-guided optimization of filter-free, camera-based thermal sensing platforms.

papers.title: Formulation Development and Evaluation of Bilayer Tablets of Metoprolol Tartrate & Indapamide Hemihydrate for the Management of Hypertension
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Hypertension is one of the most prevalent chronic cardiovascular disorders and is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality worldwide.Effective blood pressure management often requires combination therapy using antihypertensive agents with different mechanisms of action.Bilayer tablet technology provides an innovative drug delivery system by combining immediate-release and sustained-release layers in a single dosage form, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy, reducing dosing frequency, and enhancing patient compliance.The present study was undertaken to formulate and evaluate bilayer tablets of Metoprolol Tartrate and Indapamide Hemihydrate for the effective management of hypertension.Nine formulations (F1-F9) were prepared by the direct compression technique.The immediate-release layer containing Metoprolol Tartrate was formulated using different concentrations of Crospovidone as the superdisintegrant, while the sustained-release layer containing Indapamide Hemihydrate was formulated using Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC K100M) as the release-retarding polymer.The prepared powder blends were evaluated for pre-compression parameters, including angle of repose, bulk density, tapped density, Carr's compressibility index, and Hausner's ratio.The compressed bilayer tablets were further evaluated for appearance, weight variation, thickness, hardness, friability, drug content uniformity, disintegration time, in vitro dissolution, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and accelerated stability studies.Among the prepared formulations, F9 exhibited the best overall performance with acceptable physicochemical properties, rapid release of Metoprolol Tartrate within 30 minutes, and sustained release of Indapamide Hemihydrate over 12 hours.DSC analysis confirmed the compatibility of the drugs with the selected excipients, while accelerated stability studies demonstrated that the optimized formulation remained stable under ICH-recommended storage conditions.The study concluded that the optimized bilayer tablet formulation offers an effective biphasic drug-release system with the potential to improve therapeutic efficacy and patient compliance in the long-term management of hypertension.

papers.title: Phenolic Profiles of Nelumbo nucifera from Manipur Against Neurodegenerative Inflammation
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Natural phenolic compounds have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.Neuroinflammation is a pivotal factor in the etiology of neurodegenerative disorders.Although Nelumbo nucifera is widely utilized in traditional medicine for neurological ailments, its phenolic composition and the associated neuroprotective mechanisms are predominantly uninvestigated.Objective: This study sought to employ ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS) to analyze the phenolic compounds of N. nucifera from Manipur and to assess its neuroprotective potential by evaluating its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities in BV2 microglial cells activated by lipopolysaccharide (LPS).Methods: UHPLC-MS/MS was utilized to identify and quantify phenolic chemicals.The neuroprotective activity was evaluated by quantifying tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), nitric oxide (NO), and intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation.Western blotting was utilized to evaluate the expression levels of NF-κB p65, phosphorylated p38 MAPK, phosphorylated JNK, cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS).M1 (iNOS and CD86) and M2 (Arg-1, CD206, IL-4, and IL-10) markers were utilized to assess microglial polarization.Results: UHPLC-MS/MS profiling revealed that the predominant phenolic compounds were myricetin (18.64 ± 0.82 mg g⁻¹ DW), quercetin (15.27 ± 0.74 mg g⁻¹ DW), and kaempferol (11.83 ± 0.56 mg g⁻¹ DW), along with rutin, catechin, gallic acid, and chlorogenic acid.Compared to LPS-treated cells, N. nucifera extract markedly decreased the generation of TNF-α (66.17%),IL-1β (68.32%),NO (68.54%), and ROS (64.80%) at a dose of 100 μg mL⁻¹ (p < 0.001).The extract induced a phenotypic shift in microglia from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the neuroprotective M2 phenotype by enhancing the synthesis of Arg-1, CD206, IL-4, and IL-10, while significantly suppressing the activation of NF-κB p65, phosphorylated p38 MAPK, phosphorylated JNK, COX-2, and iNOS.Conclusion: The results demonstrate that N. nucifera from Manipur is a considerable source of bioactive phenolics with notable neuroprotective characteristics.The extract reduced neuroinflammation by promoting anti-inflammatory microglial polarization and lowering oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokine production, and NF-κB/MAPK signaling.These findings demonstrate N. nucifera's potential as a natural therapeutic alternative for the prevention and treatment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative illnesses, offering mechanistic validity for the plant's traditional medicinal uses.

papers.title: Metal Octoates as Lewis Acid Catalysts for the Hydrolytic Depolymerization of PET in Tetrahydrofuran
papers.abstract: Chemical recycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with decomposition into monomers suitable for resynthesizing primary polymer is a critical task for achieving carbon neutrality in the polyester industry. This paper presents a study comparing PET depolymerization solvolysis in tetrahydrofuran medium using a series of metal octoates (Co, Mn, Zn, Ca, Ba, Li, Zr, Cu, Pb). The resulting terephthalic acid (TPA) was characterized using a combination of methods (1H NMR, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, and Raman spectroscopy). In an aprotic tetrahydrofuran (THF) medium, a comparative performance of commercial metal octoates under fixed metal-mass loading was conducted for the first time: the leadership of Co (83.7%) and Pb (78.4%) is explained by the lability of their coordination sphere, while the anomalously low activity of Zr (17.5%) is associated with steric blocking of the metal active center. In the present work, the influence of technological parameters on the depolymerization process using the most active catalyst, cobalt octoate, was studied. It was found that increasing the reaction time from 1 to 6 h leads to an increase in PET conversion from 27% to ~85%, and in TPA yield from 14% to ~84%. A study of the influence of water content in the reaction mixture showed that increasing the water concentration to 20 wt.% intensifies hydrolysis, promoting an increase in the yield of TPA to ~80%; however, a further increase in the water content (up to 30 wt.%) does not lead to a significant change in the yield, which indicates the achievement of conditions providing the highest observed isolated TPA yield within the tested range for the reaction in this system. The obtained results create a scientific basis for the rational design of catalytic systems for the depolymerization of PET, adapted to the different qualities of secondary raw materials and the technological requirements of industrial chemical recycling.

papers.title: Carbon Quantum Dots‐Decorated Mn 0.5 Cd 0.5 S/BiOBr S‐Scheme Heterojunction With Interfacial Bi─S Bonding as an Efficient Piezocatalyst for Aqueous Cr(VI) Reduction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] is a serious environmental problem that needs to be removed efficiently from water without the need for reagents. A two‐step hydrothermal/solvothermal method was employed to synthesize a ternary piezocatalyst of carbon quantum dots (CDs) coupled with Mn 0.5 Cd 0.5 S (MCS) and BiOBr (BOB), denoted MBC, with an interfacial Bi─S bond and tested for the piezocatalytic reduction of Cr(VI) under dark and ultrasound‐assisted conditions. BOB microsphere architecture which was also uniformly decorated with cauliflower‐like MCS aggregates and had a systematic increase in carbon content from 12.5 to 25.9 wt.% as the nominal loading of CDs in the BOB was increased from MBC‐1 to MBC‐3. In the case of Cr(VI), all three ternary MBC composites showed significant removal efficiency of the target ion compared to the respective BOB and MCS, with MBC‐2 showing the best removal efficiency (89%), whereas the control without the catalyst removed 5.2% of the Cr(VI), which indicates that the removal of Cr(VI) is not a sonolytic effect but a true piezo‐driven effect. Based on these results, an S‐scheme charge‐transfer mechanism that involves the interface between chemically bonded Bi─S and anchored CDs is proposed.

papers.title: Addressing the burden and associated factors of undernutrition in under-five children with congenital heart disease in Pakistan: evidence from a multicenter cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at heightened risk of undernutrition due to elevated metabolic demands, feeding intolerance, and growth failure. This study aimed to identify the associated factors of undernutrition among children under 5 years with CHD in Pakistan. Methods A hospital-based study was carried out among 197 confirmed CHD across three tertiary hospitals in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). WHO-recommended standards and structured questionnaires were used. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of undernutrition. Results Overall, 58.9% were male, 40.1% were stunted, 44.2% were underweight, and 35.5% were wasted. Ventricular septal defect was the most common CHD (34.5%), followed by patent ductus arteriosus (23.4%). Infants aged 6–11 months had the most severe deficits. Male children had significantly higher odds of wasting than female children (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.10–3.98), whereas children from households with a monthly income of ≥ PKR 40,000 had lower odds of wasting (aOR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.24–0.84) and underweight (aOR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.29–0.94). Similarly, children whose fathers were government employees (aOR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.09–0.98) also had lower odds of being underweight. No sociodemographic or clinical variables were significantly associated with stunting (all p > 0.05). Conclusion Undernutrition exhibits a high distribution and severity among young CHD children. Multiple associated factors of undernutrition based on wasting and underweight were identified. Timely referrals for nutritional support are of great significance in preventing nutritional deterioration.

Results Overall, 58.9% were male, 40.1% were stunted, 44.2% were underweight, and 35.5% were wasted.

papers.title: Early Dual-path Detail Preservation for Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation with U-Net
papers.journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
papers.abstract: Thin retinal vessels can be attenuated during early encoder downsampling while contributing little to conventional overlap scores.We propose Dual-Path Detail Preservation (DPD), a low-overhead U-Net modification that retains max-pooling and adds zero-initialised, phase-resolved residuals beside the first two encoder reductions.Standard U-Net and DPD were compared over three training seeds on the official DRIVE test set and by datasetspecific out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation on STARE and subject-grouped CHASE_DB1.On DRIVE, DPD increased sensitivity from 0.8251 to 0.8377 and reduced thin-vessel false negatives by 5.52%.A two-way seed-and-case bootstrap retained confidence intervals excluding zero for sensitivity and thin-vessel false-negative reduction, whereas missed-branch and coverage effects became seed-sensitive.The primary recovery direction also persisted across 11 prespecified structural-diagnostic settings and both DRIVE manual annotations.STARE and CHASE_DB1 showed smaller, mixed, seed-dependent effects, with all two-way OOF intervals including zero.DPD adds 0.95% trainable parameters and approximately 2.70% convolutional GMACs.The evidence supports a targeted, dataset-conditional improvement in thin-vessel recovery rather than universal pixel-level superiority.

papers.title: Morphology-aware Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Using Differentiable Voronoi Graph Tokenization Framework
papers.journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
papers.abstract: Tomato plants are valuable agricultural crops that are susceptible to various diseases that require timely diagnosis to enhance crop quality and production rates.However, existing models use rigid patching, which causes structural fragmentation and discards important structural information.Furthermore, existing models inadequately represent irregular lesion regions, which are essential for differentiating between leaf diseases.To overcome these issues in tomato leaf classification, this paper proposes Differentiable Voronoi Graph Tokenization (DV-GT) framework, which maps image regions into an irregular graph representation by replacing rigid patching in the transformer model.The dual-path architecture enables the model to effectively extract both texture and spatial features using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gabor filter.Furthermore, Voronoi tokenization is used to align with high-gradient image regions, allowing the model to differentiate between diseases.The DV-GT framework utilizes a combination of a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to extract localized morphological structures and long-range, leaf-wide visual relationships.This enables the DV-GT framework to achieve a classification accuracy of 98.44% on the PlantVillage dataset and 89.47% on the PlantDoc dataset.These results indicate that the proposed DV-GT framework differentiates between visually similar classes and classifies tomato leaf diseases into multiple categories.

papers.title: Sustainable Approach to Thermoplastic Polyurethanes Stabilization: Vanillin as a Natural Additive in Melt-Processing
papers.abstract: Thermo-oxidative degradation during high-temperature processing remains a major challenge limiting the performance of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs). This study evaluated vanillin (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde), a bio-based phenolic compound, as a primary thermo-oxidative stabilizer acting as a free-radical scavenger. Bio-based TPU (bio-TPU) was synthesized via a two-step method using a commercial bio-based polyol, a bio-based chain extender, and a mixture of diisocyanates. During processing in an internal mixer, vanillin was incorporated into both bio-TPU and a commercial TPU at concentrations of 0.03, 0.165, and 0.3 wt%. Changes in chemical structure were assessed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermal properties were evaluated by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), including oxidation onset temperature (OOT) measurements, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Mechanical properties were assessed by tensile test and hardness. FTIR analysis revealed no significant structural changes after vanillin addition. However, changes in thermal properties were observed, including an increase in the OOT for materials containing the highest vanillin content. TGA results also showed a generally improved thermal stability at higher vanillin concentrations, approaching reference-material values at the highest concentration in the commercial TPU. A slight decrease in mechanical properties was observed. These findings demonstrate a pronounced stabilizing effect of 0.3 wt% vanillin on both bio-TPU and commercial TPU, providing new insights into the potential reuse and further recycling of TPU materials stabilized with bio-based additives.

Bio-based TPU (bio-TPU) was synthesized via a two-step method using a commercial bio-based polyol, a bio-based chain extender, and a mixture of diisocyanates. TGA results also showed a generally improved thermal stability at higher vanillin concentrations, approaching reference-material values at the highest concentration in the commercial TPU.

papers.title: DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF CUBOSOMAL GEL USING ANTI-FUNGAL AGENT
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The objective of the present study is to developed voriconazole loaded cubosomal gel for localized drug delivery through the skin, to improve drug bioavailability, improved therapeutic efficacy, while minimizing side effects and reducing dosing frequency. Voriconazole pre-formulation studies was carried out such as melting point, FTIR, DSC analysis, determination of wavelength, determination of calibration curve study. Cubosomal formulation were formulated by using top-down technique, were developed by using glyceryl monooleate as a lipid and poloxamer 407 as a stabilizer, Then it is formulated as a Carbopol gel base, Optimization was carried out by using 32 factorial design The optimized batch was subjected to in vitro anti-fungal activity, morphological analysis using a high resolution scanning electron microscopy, zeta potential, polydispersity index, drug content and entrapment efficiency. From F1-F9 formulations, Studies showed that F5 batch was optimized batch, a various parameters such as organoleptic properties, pH, spredability, viscosity and drug release were evaluated. The optimized cubosomal formulation exhibits a Vesicle size 10.63 nm, polydispersity index 0.254, zeta potential 0.0211 mV, % EE 92.67%. % Drug content 96.42%. The pH of gel 5.7, spreadability of 46.46 g·cm/sec, viscosity of 6674± 3.22 cps, the optimized formulation exhibits better In-vitro anti-fungal activity against Candida albicans showed a 12 mm zone of inhibition, In-vitro drug release rate 62.58% at 12 hours, Long-term stability analysis confirmed the formulation stability under cold condition. In conclusion, VRC loaded cubosomal gel presents a promising avenue to treating the skin fungal infections, offering sustained drug release and improved patient compliance.

Objective:-The general objective of this research is to evaluate the nutritional composition and the physiological effect of the pulp of the fruit of Raphia sese De Wild (Arecaceae) on the regulation of blood glucose levels.

papers.title: Design challenges and enabling technologies for ultra-high-speed electric drive systems
papers.abstract: Ultra-high-speed electric drive systems are a key route toward higher power density in electric vehicles, aerospace propulsion, and industrial applications, with series-production traction machines now exceeding 20,000 r/min and laboratory prototypes approaching or exceeding 100,000 r/min. This mini-review examines the design challenges and enabling technologies of ultra-high-speed machines, organized around five engineering questions: how high electrical frequency reshapes loss mechanisms and winding design, how centrifugal and fatigue loading constrain rotor structures, which bearing technologies remain viable at extreme speeds, how windage and cooling limit thermal management, and how power electronics and control must adapt. Findings are synthesized from peer-reviewed journal literature, with particular attention to retaining-sleeve material selection, rotor stress and balancing, active magnetic bearing systems, windage loss scaling, and direct oil cooling trade-offs. Because rotational speed alone does not define the operational limits—tip speed, electrical frequency, bearing DN values, and rated power are equally decisive—the review frames each topic around its underlying physical constraint rather than a nominal speed threshold. By identifying the conflicts among electromagnetic performance, mechanical integrity, and thermal stability, and by separating mature industrial practice from laboratory demonstrations, this review aims to provide a focused reference for researchers and engineers developing next-generation high-speed electric propulsion systems.

papers.title: Valorization of cotton waste into cellulose nanocrystals and their incorporation into electrospun poly (vinyl alcohol) nanofibrous membranes with enhanced thermal and structural properties
papers.abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration from 40% to 62% was associated with an increase in CNC yield from approximately 19.20 ± 3.9% to 41.30 ± 3.1%, indicating the influence of acid concentration on the recovery of the nanocrystalline fraction under the conditions employed. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) showed carbon and oxygen as the predominant elements, at 62.39 and 34.33 wt%, respectively, with trace amounts of sulfur and sodium. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed snowflake-like aggregated structures composed of branched rod-like features, with an average width of 56.5 ± 8.7 nm . Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed broadly consistent nanoscale morphological features, with snowflake-like structures ranging from approximately 120–200 nm and protruding branches of approximately 63.2 ± 10.9 nm in diameter. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed characteristic cellulose bands, including the band at 872.9 cm⁻¹ associated with β-(1→4)-glycosidic linkages. CNCs were incorporated into poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA) nanofibrous membranes at concentrations of 0–40 wt% via electrospinning. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) of the 40 wt% CNC membrane revealed a relatively uniform fibrous network with a mean fiber diameter of 104.3 ± 38.6 nm, with CNCs distributed on the fiber surfaces. FTIR analysis of the prepared nanofibers showed the characteristic 916 cm⁻¹ band, supporting the presence of the cellulose component. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed an increase in residual mass with increasing CNC content, from 1.28% for the neat PVA membrane to 24.88% for the 40 wt% CNC membrane. Derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content. The 40 wt% CNC formulation exhibited the highest residual mass among the studied formulations. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes.
papers.summary: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis. Derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes.

papers.title: Esketamine alleviates the pain-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex
papers.abstract: Objective The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine (ESK) efficacy in the pain-depression dyad (PDD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of a sub-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Methods Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD + ESK groups. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury (CCI), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression-like phenotypes. On day 21 post-surgery, PDD + ESK rats received a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg, i.p.). Multi-regional c-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations (including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting. Results ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats. Regional c-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα-positive neurons. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling (unadjusted P < 0.05) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure. Conclusion A single sub-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain-related affective disorders.

Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure.

papers.title: Technological gaps and green efficiency in urban agglomerations: evidence from China and the United States
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
papers.abstract: This study benchmarks green efficiency in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) in China and the San Francisco Bay Area (SFBA) in the United States to diagnose whether emerging megaregions' green gap reflects managerial inefficiency or technological backwardness. Using a Slacks-Based Measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs within a meta-frontier framework, it decomposes Meta-Frontier Efficiency (MTE) into Group Technical Efficiency (GTE) and the Technology Gap Ratio (TGR) for 35 cities and counties over 2004 to 2023. The two agglomerations achieve nearly identical managerial efficiency, with average GTE of 0.920 and 0.914, but the SFBA's MTE of 0.920 far exceeds the YRD's 0.795. This gap stems from technology: the SFBA's TGR is 1.000, meaning its group frontier coincides with the global meta-frontier, whereas the YRD's TGR is only 0.873 and has widened over time. Spatial autocorrelation analysis reveals no significant clustering of green productivity, indicating that green technologies are highly localized and do not diffuse spontaneously across city boundaries, so that economic integration has outpaced environmental and technological integration. These findings imply that the YRD should shift its policy focus from managerial tightening toward green technology research and development, and promote policy-driven green technology transfer from leading cities to peripheral manufacturing ones.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions and the cGAS–STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action
papers.abstract: Research on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-related interventions has shifted from overall phenotypic effects to defined neuroimmune targets. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) axis connects cytosolic DNA sensing with host defense and sterile inflammatory injury, but the functional direction of this pathway changes with disease context. This review organizes preclinical findings by pathological setting and site of action. It examines herbal formulas and natural compounds, followed by acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and related delivery systems. Several sterile injury models associate benefit with reduced pathway-related inflammation. Acute sleep deprivation provides an example of protection accompanying restored STING signaling. Early herpes simplex virus infection follows a different pattern: restoration of suppressed antiviral signaling improves host defense. In acute postoperative pain and cancer-induced bone pain models, increased STING-IFN-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture-induced analgesia. Some interventions reduce mitochondrial DNA stimulation. Others act on cGAS or STING, with separate studies targeting STING trafficking. Downstream inflammatory and cell-death responses form the final level. Mechanistic attribution is strongest when genetic or pharmacological perturbation links pathway change to functional outcome; direct binding has been demonstrated for a small group of compounds. These findings support a context-sensitive framework for interpreting modulation direction that requires validation within individual disease models. Clinical translation will depend on reproducible formulation composition, effective brain exposure, and safety.

Mechanistic attribution is strongest when genetic or pharmacological perturbation links pathway change to functional outcome; direct binding has been demonstrated for a small group of compounds. Clinical translation will depend on reproducible formulation composition, effective brain exposure, and safety.

papers.title: Concentration‐Dependent Lamellar Organization and Structure–Property Relationships in Melt‐Processed EVA /Cloisite 20A Nanocomposites
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of Cloisite 20A content (0–7.5 wt%) on the structural organization and thermomechanical behavior of melt‐processed EVA nanocomposites was systematically evaluated, with emphasis on clay dispersion and lamellar arrangement. X‐ray diffraction revealed a concentration‐dependent shift of the (001) peak, indicating a transition from highly disordered lamellae at low clay loadings to predominantly intercalated structures with partial restacking at higher concentrations. Transmission electron microscopy corroborated this evolution, showing more dispersed platelets at 2.5% and increased tactoid formation at 5.0% and 7.5%, confirming the progressive reorganization of the silicate galleries during processing. Differential scanning calorimetry showed that the EVA melting temperature remained essentially unchanged, whereas crystallinity was strongly influenced by clay morphology. At low and intermediate loadings, restricted chain mobility was observed, whereas at higher concentrations a nucleating effect occurred, associated with increased interfacial density. Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed the preservation of the dual degradation mechanism, with slight shifts in characteristic temperatures due to interfacial effects. Young's modulus increased with clay addition, while tensile strength and ductility exhibited moderate reductions. Overall, the results demonstrate that nanostructural organization governs the balance among stiffness, thermal stability, and toughness, defining an optimal compositional window.

papers.title: The impact of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions: an empirical examination based on Chinese urban panel data
papers.abstract: Depressive emotions have emerged as a critical public health concern, with their etiology closely linked to the natural environment, particularly air quality. Grounded in environmental stress theory and social support theory, this study utilizes panel data from 277 prefecture-level cities in China spanning 2011–2023 to theoretically analyze and empirically examine the effects of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions and the underlying mechanisms. The findings reveal that: First, improvements in air quality significantly reduce public attention to depressive emotions, a conclusion that remains robust across multiple robustness tests. Second, the unemployment rate serves as a partial mediator between air quality and public attention to depressive emotions, while healthcare workforce allocation and public fiscal expenditure effectively buffer the adverse psychological impacts of air quality deterioration. Third, the influence of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions exhibits significant urban heterogeneity, being more pronounced in eastern and central regions, cities with net population outflows, and mature and declining resource-based cities. By examining environmental public goods and social support systems, this study provides novel empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between air quality and public mental health, offering valuable insights for promoting synergy between environmental policies and social security policies.

papers.title: Response-Surface-Guided Extraction and Copper Modification of Nanocellulose from Corn Cob and Hemp Hurds: Source- and Loading-Dependent Structural and Electrochemical Properties
papers.abstract: Agricultural residues offer a source of nanocellulose for developing functional composites. This study examined how biomass source, extraction conditions, and copper loading affect the structural and electrochemical properties of nanocellulose derived from hemp hurds and corn cob. A citric-acid-assisted chemical–mechanical extraction route was investigated using response surface methodology, with extraction cycle number and sonication time as factors and FTIR-derived total crystallinity index and SEM-derived apparent fiber size as responses. The selected conditions were three cycles and 120 min for hemp hurds and three cycles and 75 min for corn cob, yielding measured mean apparent fiber sizes of 83.3 and 100 nm, respectively. Nanocellulose was modified with nominal Cu loadings of 15, 25, 50, and 75 wt%. At 0.1 Hz, impedance magnitude decreased from 274.15 and 247.67 kΩ for the respective bare references to below 10 kΩ for all Cu-modified groups. Cu incorporation also increased cycle-5 passed charge, with the corn-cob series showing its highest mean response at 50 wt%. FTIR, SEM, TGA, and XRD supported cellulose enrichment, nanoscale fibrillation, source-dependent thermal behavior, and crystalline metallic Cu formation. These findings support further evaluation of Cu-modified nanocellulose for electrochemical applications.

A citric-acid-assisted chemical–mechanical extraction route was investigated using response surface methodology, with extraction cycle number and sonication time as factors and FTIR-derived total crystallinity index and SEM-derived apparent fiber size as responses. These findings support further evaluation of Cu-modified nanocellulose for electrochemical applications.

papers.title: Pan-genome analysis reveals conservation and diversification of the SWEET gene family in wheat
papers.abstract: SWEET (Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporter) proteins mediate sugar transport and play important roles in plant growth, development, source-sink allocation, and responses to environmental stimuli. However, the conservation and diversification of the SWEET gene family across the wheat pan-genome remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic pan-genome analysis of the SWEET gene family across 19 hexaploid wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) accessions. A total of 1,594 SWEET genes were identified, with 77–90 members in individual genomes. Gene copies belonging to core, soft-core, dispensable, and private homologous groups accounted for 52.6%, 30.9%, 14.6%, and 1.9%, respectively, based on presence/absence variation (PAV), revealing a predominantly conserved genomic framework accompanied by a smaller accession-variable component. Phylogenetic, motif, chromosomal and synteny analyses further revealed extensive evolutionary and genomic conservation accompanied by localized diversification among family members. Extensive homeologous and inter-accession collinearity was observed, and most pairwise ortholog comparisons exhibited Ka/Ks ratios below 1, supporting predominant purifying selection on conserved SWEET coding sequences. Promoter analysis identified diverse putative cis-regulatory elements related to environmental, hormonal, and developmental regulation, while transcriptome profiling showed heterogeneous tissue- and stress-associated expression patterns among TaSWEET genes. qRT-PCR analysis further suggested distinct temporal responses of selected TaSWEET genes under cold and polyethylene glycol (PEG)-induced osmotic stress. TaSWEET47 overexpression significantly increased grain width, thousand-grain weight, and mature-grain starch content in two independent transgenic lines without significantly affecting grain length. Collectively, these results reveal gene-content, evolutionary, regulatory, and transcriptional diversification within a broadly conserved SWEET family framework.

papers.title: Electrochemical and Mechanical Understanding of Extruded and Solvent‐Cast Solid Polymer Electrolytes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on Poly(ethylene oxide)‐Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PEO–LiTFSI) are promising materials for solid‐state batteries. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted on their electrochemical and mechanical properties, with SPEs prepared via two processing methods: extrusion and solvent casting. The effects of Al 2 O 3 addition and membrane thickness on SPE performance and cyclability were investigated. Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al 2 O 3 improved membrane stability. Thicker membranes exhibited larger polarization gradients, slower ion diffusion, and lower Sand times, leading to reduced electrochemical performance. Mechanical properties, including yield stress, storage modulus, and fracture toughness, were assessed using rheology and dynamic mechanical analysis. Extruded SPEs displayed higher stiffness and greater resistance to dendrite formation than solvent‐cast membranes. Monotonic crack growth tests indicated that the presence of Al 2 O 3 increased fracture toughness, enhancing crack resistance and potentially extending cycle life. Overall, membranes produced via extrusion, containing Al 2 O 3 , and optimized for reduced thickness, combined superior electrochemical properties, making them strong candidates for solid‐state battery applications, as demonstrated by their incorporation in multilayer cells.

Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al 2 O 3 improved membrane stability. papers.title: Effect of Temperature on Piezoresistive Behaviour of Carbon Nanotube Filled Epoxy Nanocomposite Strain Sensors sQRS
papers.abstract: The incorporation of composite materials in structural applications is experiencing significant growth, with structures such as composite wind turbine blades now reaching 100 m in length and operating under increasingly demanding environmental conditions, including broad temperature ranges. Reliable structural health monitoring (SHM) based on quantum piezoresistive strain sensors (sQRS) therefore requires a thorough understanding of how temperature affects the sensor’s response. In this study, we investigate the effect of temperature, from 25 °C to 150 °C, on the electrical and piezoresistive behaviour of epoxy-based carbon nanotube (CNT) sensors intended for integration into composite structures. We show that below the glass transition temperature (Tg ≈ 95–100 °C, determined by dynamic mechanical analysis) of the epoxy matrix, the sensor’s resistance decreases reversibly and near-instantaneously with temperature, governed by enhanced tunnelling conduction competing with matrix thermal expansion. Under mechanical loading, this thermal sensitivity translates into a marked, though still usable, decrease in gauge factor (56% between −30 °C and 80 °C), attributed to reduced stress transfer and increasing matrix Poisson’s ratio. Above Tg, the sensor’s response becomes irreversible: matrix softening enables dynamic percolation and permanent reorganisation of the CNT network, leading to a substantial, non-recoverable loss of piezoresistive sensitivity. These findings identify Tg as the practical operational limit for reliable strain sensing with sQRS, and demonstrate that below this limit, temperature-induced resistance drift is linear and readily compensated, making the sensor’s thermal response itself a potential tool for in situ detection of the matrix’s physical state.

papers.title: Association between infertility prevalence and exposure to heat stress: an ecological study based on the Universal Thermal Climate Index
papers.abstract: Background Repeated exposure to heat stress may adversely affect reproductive health, yet the population-level relationship between heat stress and infertility has not been well characterized. Methods We conducted a global ecological analysis across 174 countries and regions from 1990 to 2021. Heat exposure was quantified as the annual number of days falling into four Universal Thermal Climate Index categories: moderate, strong, very strong, and extreme heat stress. We additionally constructed a weighted score combining very strong and extreme heat stress. Associations with male and female infertility prevalence were estimated using linear mixed-effects models. Results Each additional day of very strong and extreme heat stress was associated with increases in male infertility ASPR of 1.292 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.675–1.908) and 1.654 (95% CI: 0.214–3.096) per 100,000 population, respectively. The corresponding increases in female infertility ASPR were 2.126 (95% CI: 0.785–3.467) and 7.133 (95% CI: 3.940–10.323) per 100,000 population, respectively. Higher weighted heat-stress scores were also consistently associated with greater infertility prevalence. Conclusions These findings suggest that recurrent heat-stress exposure may be associated with a higher population burden of infertility and support consideration of reproductive health in climate-change adaptation and heat-protection strategies.

Results Each additional day of very strong and extreme heat stress was associated with increases in male infertility ASPR of 1.292 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.675–1.908) and 1.654 (95% CI: 0.214–3.096) per 100,000 population, respectively. Conclusions These findings suggest that recurrent heat-stress exposure may be associated with a higher population burden of infertility and support consideration of reproductive health in climate-change adaptation and heat-protection strategies.

papers.title: Valorization of Bio- and Coal-Based Ash in Rigid Polyurethane Foams: Thermomechanical Performance and Decomposition Under Pyrolytic Conditions
papers.abstract: This study investigates the pyrolytic processes and thermomechanical properties of polyurethane (PU) foamed composites filled with ashes obtained after sunflower husk combustion and conventional coal combustion, as well as their silanized derivatives. The results indicate that an improvement in thermal stability during the initial stages of pyrolysis was observed only for PU composites containing silanized ash generated from conventional coal combustion (a difference of 5 °C). At later stages of the thermal decomposition, a significant increase in temperature resistance was observed for the remaining composites. Kinetic studies of degradation using isoconversional methods revealed that composites containing sunflower husk ash exhibit degradation mechanisms different from those of the reference material, as observed by the changes in the activation energy particularly within the conversion range of 0.40–0.65. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) demonstrated that all composites show improved mechanical response over a broad temperature range, with the highest mechanical performance observed after ash silanization (doubled E′ at the initial stage of the study compared to the reference). The analysis of evolved gases, performed using the Py-GC/MS technique, proved the existence of a different degradation path for composites with sunflower husk ash by a change in the amount of evolved gases during the pyrolysis process.

papers.title: 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride based polymer electrolytes for supercapacitor applications
papers.abstract: The aim of this work was to investigate the effect of 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (BMIMCI) on the structural, electrical, and electrochemical properties of PVDF-HFP/NaI solid polymer electrolyte for supercapacitor applications. In this work, solid polymer electrolyte films were prepared using the solution casting method with Polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene (PVDF-HFP) as the host polymer. Sodium iodide salt (NaI) and an ionic liquid, 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (BMIMCI) was incorporated in different weight percentages to improve ionic conductivity. The maximum conductivity of 8.07 × 10 − 4 S/cm was achieved at 4% BMIMCI. The ionic transference number (t ion ) was found to be 0.92, indicates that the ions mainly take part in the conduction process. Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) revealed a wide electrochemical stability window of 3.67 V, making the electrolyte suitable for practical applications. Surface morphology of the films was studied using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Polarized Optical Microscopy (POM), which showed a more uniform and less crystalline structure after the addition of the ionic liquid, supporting enhanced ion movement. Differential scanning calorimetry study showed a decrease in crystallinity and an increase in amorphous nature, helping easier movement if ions inside the polymer electrolyte. The optimized solid polymer electrolyte films was further used to fabricate a supercapacitor device. The device exhibited a specific capacitance of 26.3 F/g. Galvanostatic charge-discharge analysis gave a maximum specific capacitance of 10.1Fg − 1 , a coulombic efficiency of 98%, an energy density of 3.9 Whkg − 1 , and a power density of 2650 Wkg − 1 . The device retained about 95% of its initial specific capacitance after 1000 charge-discharge cycles, indicating good cycling stability, showing good electrochemical performance.

The device retained about 95% of its initial specific capacitance after 1000 charge-discharge cycles, indicating good cycling stability, showing good electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Comparative efficacy of brain-computer interface training with different feedback modalities for post-stroke upper-limb motor recovery: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.abstract: Background Brain-computer interface (BCI) training may improve post-stroke upper-limb recovery through closed-loop feedback, but the comparative efficacy of different feedback modalities remains uncertain. This study compared BCI training with different feedback modalities for post-stroke upper-limb motor impairment. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched from inception through April 2026 for randomized controlled trials of BCI-based upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke. BCI interventions were classified by feedback modality and feedback contingency into multimodal feedback (BCI-MM), robotic or exoskeleton-assisted feedback (BCI-Robot), functional electrical stimulation feedback (BCI-FES), and visual feedback (BCI-visual), while comparator interventions were classified separately, with usual rehabilitation (UR) as the reference. Random-effects network meta-analysis estimated WMDs with 95% CIs. The primary outcome was Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE); secondary outcomes were the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) and Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty was assessed using CINeMA. Results Twenty-two trials involving 956 patients across subacute, chronic, and mixed post-stroke stages were included. The FMA-UE network contained 11 connected nodes, with no global or local inconsistency. Compared with UR, BCI-Robot showed greater FMA-UE improvement (WMD = 6.28, 95% CI 2.70–9.86), as did non-BCI robotic training (WMD = 4.26, 95% CI 0.42–8.10) and BCI-MM (WMD = 4.03, 95% CI 1.00–7.06). BCI-FES did not differ significantly from UR. BCI-visual had the highest SUCRA value (77.6%), but its comparison with UR was non-significant, with very low certainty of evidence; no BCI feedback modality was superior to another. Secondary outcomes showed greater ARAT improvement with BCI-Robot versus UR, whereas WMFT findings were non-significant. Certainty for the main FMA-UE comparisons was low or very low. Conclusion BCI-Robot and BCI-MM showed statistically significant FMA-UE benefits versus UR, although certainty was low. As non-BCI robotic training also showed benefit, the BCI-Robot effect cannot be attributed to BCI alone. No BCI feedback modality was statistically superior to another. Further high-quality direct-comparison trials are needed. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261370474 , Unique Identifier: CRD420261370474.
papers.summary: Background Brain-computer interface (BCI) training may improve post-stroke upper-limb recovery through closed-loop feedback, but the comparative efficacy of different feedback modalities remains uncertain. Conclusion BCI-Robot and BCI-MM showed statistically significant FMA-UE benefits versus UR, although certainty was low. As non-BCI robotic training also showed benefit, the BCI-Robot effect cannot be attributed to BCI alone.

papers.title: Influence of sonication duration pretreatment on thermal degradation behavior and pyrolysis kinetics of raw and pretreated spent mushroom substrate (SMS)
papers.abstract: This study reveals that sonication-assisted acid leaching, particularly with a 20-min sonication duration (SMS20), offers a highly effective pretreatment method for Spent Mushroom Substrate (SMS), significantly reducing its ash content and enhancing its suitability as a bioenergy feedstock. While SMS is a promising bioenergy resource, its high alkali and alkaline earth metal (AAEM) content leads to elevated ash levels, causing operational challenges such as slagging, fouling, and reduced pyrolysis efficiency. Previous kinetics studies often overlooked the comprehensive thermal degradation behavior across all major decomposition stages. Therefore, this study investigated the effect of sonication-assisted acid leaching on the thermal degradation behavior and activation energy of SMS across three decomposition sections corresponding to moisture removal, hemicellulose degradation, and cellulose degradation. The ash content was significantly reduced from 19.766 %, in raw SMS to 5.161% in the SMS20 sample, while volatile matter increased to 72.286%, indicating enhanced thermal reactivity. Thermal analysis revealed four distinct degradation regions: moisture removal (30–61 °C), hemicellulose decomposition (140–280 °C), and cellulose decomposition (280–360 °C), Char formation (700-1000 °C). Activation energy analysis showed that the pretreatment reduced the energy required for moisture removal and cellulose degradation. In the hemicellulose region, activation energy varied among the pretreated samples, indicating that the pretreatment altered the thermal stability of this fraction depending on the sonication duration. Notably, SMS20 exhibited the lowest activation energy in both the hemicellulose and cellulose regions, demonstrating the highest thermal reactivity among all samples. These findings confirm that a 20-min sonication-assisted acid leaching pretreatment is the optimum condition for enhancing the pyrolysis performance of SMS for thermochemical conversion by minimizing ash content and improving pyrolysis characteristics. Schematic workflow of the pyrolysis of acid-leached Spent Mushroom Substrate (SMS). the process involves biomass preparation (drying, grinding, and sieving to 250 µm), followed by 1% HNO3 acid leaching assisted by sonication (5–25 min). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was employed to characterize the thermal decomposition stages (moisture, volatiles, fixed carbon, and ash). Kinetic parameters, including activation energy (Ea) and pre-exponential factor (A), were determined using the Coats-Redfern integral method through linear regression of ln[-ln(1-α)/T2] versus 1/T. This schematic diagram was generated using Manus AI.

papers.title: Development of Supramolecular Calix[4]arene-MCM-Based Nanomaterials Doped with CuNPs: An Inorganic–Organic Hybrid Recyclable Nanoenzyme as a Potent Peroxidase and Oxidase Mimic
papers.abstract: Abstract An inorganic–organic hybrid nanomaterial, Cu@MCMCal, was synthesized by immobilizing p-tert-butyl calix[4]arene on to mesoporous silica followed by incorporation of CuNPs. The synthesized nanomaterial was characterized extensively using various analytical techniques such as FT-IR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, TEM, PXRD, XPS, Cu LMM Auger, BET, and TGA analyses. The hybrid nanomaterial was evaluated for its catalytic performance toward peroxidase-like activity using 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and o-phenylenediamine (OPD) as a substrate at room temperature at pH 4.5 in acetate buffer and pH 7.4 in PBS buffer, respectively. Enzyme kinetics was performed for both the substrates using the Michaelis–Menten steady-state kinetics and the Lineweaver–Burk plot to determine the catalytic affinity. Based on the kinetic measurements, the values of the Km for TMB and OPD were found to be 0.661 ± 0.143 and 0.606 ± 0.061 mM, respectively. The hybrid nanoenzyme also exhibits the oxidase-like activity using dopamine as a substrate at pH 7.4 in PBS buffer. The Cu@MCMCal nanomaterial acted as a nanoenzyme, efficient for catalysis toward oxidation reactions with better cost effectiveness and improved stability and recyclability as compared to biological enzymes. Therefore, a promising, stable, efficient, and robust nanoenzyme has been development for oxidation reactions.
